tldr: This paper transforms the semidefinite program for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of bounds for large measurement sets.
motivation: The standard SDP for deciding joint measurability and steering becomes intractable for large measurement sets due to exponential growth in variables and constraints.
method: The authors develop a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements, applicable to arbitrary POVMs.
result: For qubits, the method yields accurate bounds for sets with hundreds of measurements quickly; for qutrits, non-trivial bounds are obtained where SDP is intractable. The approach also constructs local hidden state models for steering.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering in large scenarios, outperforming standard SDP in scalability.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: This paper tightly characterizes the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for all parameter regimes.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine in quantum computing, but its cost when given imperfect advice (states with partial overlap with the top eigenspace) was not well understood. Understanding this helps in designing more efficient quantum algorithms.
method: The authors develop algorithms for phase estimation with advice and prove lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, as well as reductions from the unitary recurrence time problem.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies do not significantly help, and that having many copies does not reduce cost much either. They also derive a tight bound for error probability reduction in basic phase estimation.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the cost of phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering insights into the power of quantum advice in this context.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states maximally violate it and linking Bell violation to Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because stabilizer states and Clifford operators do not produce violations for qudits; the paper aims to find a qudit Bell inequality that connects nonlocality to Wigner negativity.
method: The authors introduce a new CHSH-like inequality for qudits using correlations related to Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalized π/8 gate, and analyze the Bell operator's relation to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specific stabilizer state achieves maximal violation among all qudit states, and the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume. Additionally, bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity serve as contextuality witnesses.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between nonlocality and Wigner negativity in qudit systems, providing a new tool for studying higher-dimensional quantum correlations.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to design sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security, starting from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols.
motivation: Device-independent security is crucial for quantum cryptography, and sequential scenarios can enhance performance by reusing quantum states.
method: Replace one measurement in a bipartite self-testing protocol with a non-projective counterpart and add an additional user, then prove security analytically.
result: The constructed ideal correlations are secure against statistical mixture reproduction, enabling device-independent certification of randomness.
conclusion: The general recipe facilitates development of new device-independent quantum security schemes.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: A fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for verifying entanglement but typically require different measurement settings. This work aims to simplify the process by using a fixed measurement setting on a specially prepared network state.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including those for bound entangled states. They extend the approach to multipartite graph states.
result: They show that decomposable EWs (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) can be estimated with a fixed setting, and non-decomposable EWs for bound entanglement are also accessible. The method applies to graph states and distributed settings.
conclusion: This measurement-based approach simplifies entanglement verification and is applicable to multipartite states and quantum networks, offering practical advantages for experiments.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time using hierarchical cellular automata, solving the open problem of a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.
motivation: Topological quantum memories require decoders that are both local and fault-tolerant; previous constructions required non-local classical processing or higher dimensions.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder preserves a logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise without non-local classical computation or communication.
conclusion: Demonstrates that a local topological quantum memory is possible in 2D, solving a long-standing open problem.

title: Catalytic Entanglement Transformations With Noisy Hardware
authors: Hemant Sharma, Aleksandr Mokeev, Jonas Helsen, And Johannes Borregaard
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2117 (2026).

The availability of certain entangled resource states (catalyst states) can enhance the rate of converting several less entangled states into fewer highly entangled states in a process known as catalytic entanglement concentration (EC). Here, we extend catalytic EC from pure states to mixed states and numerically benchmark it against non-catalytic EC and distillation in the presence of state-preparation errors and operational errors. Furthermore, we analyse the re-usability of catalysts in the presence of such errors. To do this, we introduce a novel recipe for determining the positive-operator valued measurements (POVM) required for EC transformations, which allows for making tradeoffs between the number of communication rounds and the number of auxiliary qubits required. We find that in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise, catalytic EC can provide better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC.

.
tldr: Extends catalytic entanglement concentration to mixed states with noisy hardware, demonstrating improved rates over distillation.
motivation: Catalytic entanglement can enhance conversion rates, but prior work focused on pure states; practical implementations require handling noise.
method: Introduces a novel POVM construction for catalytic EC, enabling tradeoffs between communication rounds and auxiliary qubits, and benchmarks against non-catalytic EC and distillation under depolarizing noise.
result: Catalytic EC achieves better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC in low operational error and depolarizing noise regimes.
conclusion: Catalytic entanglement transformations are viable on noisy hardware and can outperform standard distillation protocols.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: This paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox by linking it to strong contextuality in the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum reasoning by agents.
motivation: The Frauchiger–Renner paradox highlights inconsistencies in quantum theory when describing itself, but its reliance on post-selection and agent reasoning has been criticized. The authors aim to provide a cleaner paradox based on logical contextuality.
method: The authors observe that the FR paradox is a manifestation of logical contextuality à la Hardy, and then construct a stronger paradox using the GHZ–Mermin scenario, which is known to be strongly contextual.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox does not require post-selection or agents reasoning about other agents quantumly, yet still yields a contradiction when assuming quantum theory is universally valid.
conclusion: The paradox reinforces the need to reconsider the consistency of quantum theory with itself, and suggests extending Peres's dictum to resolve extended Wigner's friend scenarios.

title: Optimal Control Of Engineered Swift Equilibration Of Nanomechanical Oscillators
authors: Julia Sanders And Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi
abstract: Processes conveying physical information are always subject to speed limits. We explore the consequence of this in optimal control of indicators of finite-time thermodynamic transitions of nano-systems evolving according to an underdamped dynamics. Our main finding is that, in the presence of speed limits, problems like optimal engineered swift equilibration and transitions towards an out-of-equilibrium state at minimum work done to the system are well-posed. In particular, we show that there is no need for discontinuities in the internal energy at the end of the control horizon. This was a problem that raised doubts for a long time on the physical meaning of certain optimal transitions. We perform our analysis on the experimentally relevant case of nano-oscillators, and we expect our predictions on optimal protocols and the evolution of mean heat and work to be experimentally testable.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control of engineered swift equilibration for nanomechanical oscillators under speed limits, showing that discontinuities in internal energy are unnecessary.
motivation: Processes conveying physical information are subject to speed limits, and optimal control of finite-time thermodynamic transitions in nano-systems is important for understanding work and heat at the nanoscale.
method: The authors analyze underdamped dynamics of nanomechanical oscillators and apply optimal control theory to find protocols that achieve swift equilibration with minimum work, considering speed limits.
result: They show that optimal engineered swift equilibration and transitions to out-of-equilibrium states are well-posed without requiring discontinuities in internal energy, resolving a long-standing doubt.
conclusion: The predicted optimal protocols and evolution of mean heat and work are experimentally testable, advancing the understanding of thermodynamic speed limits in nano-systems.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel QMC algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the 2nd Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results match the theoretical value for the corner logarithmic term at the Gaussian tricritical point, and also yield consistent results along the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The algorithm establishes a long-sought connection between universal values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes in (2+1)d.

title: Scalable Acceleration Of Many-Body Quantum Dynamics Via Time-Rescaling
authors: Edson B. de Almeida Filho, \^angelo F. Da Silva Fran\c{c}a, Bert\'ulio de Lima Bernardo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast quantum control is essential to overcome decoherence in contemporary quantum platforms, yet achieving this in many-body systems remains a major challenge. We show that the time-rescaling (TR) method enables efficient acceleration of closed many-body quantum dynamics, extending its applicability beyond previously studied regimes. Applying TR to the transverse-field Ising model with a longitudinal field, we demonstrate a significant enhancement of quantum annealing performance, maintaining high ground-state fidelity at evolution times where standard adiabatic dynamics breaks down, with only weak dependence on system size. We further demonstrate high-fidelity preparation of Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states in many-body systems, where TR extends the accessible system sizes within fixed evolution times. We additionally show that the Mandelstam-Tamm quantum speed limit does not fundamentally limit the acceleration achievable through TR, as the reduction in evolution time is exactly compensated by increased energy fluctuations. These results establish TR as a scalable and experimentally viable approach to fast quantum control in many-body systems.
tldr: The paper shows that time-rescaling (TR) method accelerates many-body quantum dynamics, enhancing quantum annealing and GHZ state preparation while circumventing the Mandelstam-Tamm speed limit.
motivation: Fast quantum control is needed to overcome decoherence, but accelerating many-body dynamics is challenging. The authors aim to extend the TR method to many-body systems.
method: They apply the TR method to the transverse-field Ising model with a longitudinal field, analyzing quantum annealing performance and GHZ state preparation via numerical simulations.
result: TR significantly improves ground-state fidelity in quantum annealing with weak system-size dependence, enables high-fidelity GHZ state preparation for larger systems, and shows that the quantum speed limit is not a fundamental barrier.
conclusion: TR is a scalable and experimentally viable approach for fast quantum control in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Memory And Thermal Amplification In Spin--cavity Squared Commutators
authors: Yong-Hong Ma, Hui-Hui Xu, Jian-Zhuang Wu, Quan-Zhen Ding, Wu-Ming Liu, Xin-Yu Zhao, E Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Squared commutators in the Holstein--Primakoff limit of a spin--cavity system provide a compact way to separate propagation from covariance growth in a finite-temperature reservoir with memory. In the finite-temperature NMQSD construction, the linear quadrature commutator is fixed by the retarded spin--cavity propagator, whereas a quadratic commutator carries the same retarded factor together with a covariance factor. For a zero-mean Gaussian state, \(C_{R_i^2,R_j}(t)=4|\kappa_{ij}(t)|^2V_{ii}(t)\); the symmetrized expression gives the spin-side and mixed channels. Since \(\bar n\) enters the covariance sector but not the homogeneous retarded kernel, raising \(\bar n\) from 0 to 1 leaves the linear transfer unchanged while increasing the quadratic signal. Varying the bath-memory rate and the counter-rotating coupling within the stable HP region then shows how stored cavity history changes both the transfer weight and its distribution in time. The calculation separates memory-dependent propagation from thermal covariance growth in collective spin--cavity dynamics.
tldr: This paper analyzes memory and thermal amplification in a spin-cavity system using squared commutators within the Holstein-Primakoff limit.
motivation: Understanding how finite-temperature reservoirs with memory affect quantum dynamics is crucial for hybrid quantum systems, particularly spin ensembles coupled to cavities.
method: The authors employ the finite-temperature NMQSD (Non-Markovian Quantum State Diffusion) formalism to separate memory-dependent propagation from thermal covariance growth, deriving expressions for linear and quadratic commutators.
result: They find that increasing the thermal photon number enhances the quadratic signal without affecting linear transfer, and that bath-memory rate and counter-rotating coupling modulate the transfer weight and its temporal distribution.
conclusion: The work provides a compact framework to analyze memory effects and thermal noise in spin-cavity systems, relevant for quantum information processing with hybrid platforms.

title: Factorization Through Lorentz Cones
authors: Guillaume Aubrun, Francesca la Piana, Alexander M\"uller-Hermes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A pair of proper cones [MATH] is said to have the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) if every [MATH]-positive map factors through a direct sum of Lorentzian cones, i.e., cones over Euclidean balls. Clearly, [MATH] has the LFP if either [MATH] or [MATH] is a direct sum of Lorentzian cones, and our main goal is to find other examples. We show that such examples cannot be found for pairs [MATH] where [MATH], or in the case where both [MATH] and [MATH] are polyhedral. We also focus on the case where [MATH] is the square-based cone in [MATH]. Here, we show that [MATH] has the LFP whenever [MATH] is a symmetric cone, i.e., a direct sum of Lorentz cones, cones of positive semidefinite matrices over the real numbers, complex numbers or quaternions, and the cone of [MATH] positive semidefinite matrices over the octonions. We leave open the question whether there are more examples, but we show that this list cannot be extended by any strictly convex cone [MATH] or for a cone [MATH] with [MATH]. Finally, we discuss an application to a problem in quantum information theory.
tldr: This paper studies the Lorentz factorization property for proper cones and applies it to a problem in quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding when positive maps factor through Lorentzian cones is a structural question with implications for quantum information, particularly in the study of entanglement and positive maps.
method: The authors define the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) and characterize pairs of cones that satisfy it, using convex geometry and cone theory. They prove impossibility results for certain cone dimensions and polyhedral cones, and show that symmetric cones have LFP when paired with a square-based cone.
result: The paper provides a complete characterization for certain cone pairs, showing that LFP holds for symmetric cones with a square-based cone, and fails for many other cases. An application to quantum information is discussed.
conclusion: The Lorentz factorization property is a new structural concept that connects convex geometry to quantum information, and the results suggest further open questions about its scope.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) for pairs of proper cones, a concept from convex geometry with applications in quantum information theory. A pair (C1, C2) has the LFP if every positive map from C1 to C2 factors through a direct sum of Lorentzian cones (cones over Euclidean balls). The authors aim to find non-trivial examples beyond the obvious case where one cone is itself a direct sum of Lorentzian cones. They prove that no such examples exist when C1 = C2, or when both cones are polyhedral. Focusing on the square-based cone C_□ in R^3, they show that (C_□, C) has the LFP if and only if C is a symmetric cone (direct sum of Lorentz cones, positive semidefinite cones over reals, complexes, quaternions, or the 3x3 octonionic cone). They also prove that this list cannot be extended by any strictly convex cone C or any cone of dimension ≤5. The paper concludes with an application to quantum information theory, specifically to the problem of characterizing cones that allow for a certain type of entanglement detection.
key_contributions: Defines the Lorentz factorization property (LFP) for pairs of proper cones and establishes its basic properties.
Proves that (C1, C2) has the LFP only in trivial cases when C1 = C2 or both are polyhedral.
Characterizes all cones C such that (C_□, C) has the LFP: exactly the symmetric cones.
Shows that the list of cones C with (C_□, C) having LFP cannot be extended by any strictly convex cone or any cone of dimension ≤5.
Provides an application to quantum information theory, linking LFP to the existence of certain entanglement witnesses.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a combination of convex geometry, cone theory, and algebraic methods. The authors use the concept of positive maps between cones and factorizations through Lorentzian cones. They leverage known classifications of symmetric cones and properties of the square-based cone. The proofs involve constructing explicit counterexamples for non-symmetric cones, using techniques such as examining the automorphism group of the cone and analyzing the structure of extreme rays. The paper also uses duality and the notion of cone isomorphisms to reduce the problem to simpler cases. The application to quantum information is presented via a mapping between cones and sets of quantum states, using the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is a complete characterization of cones C for which (C_□, C) has the LFP: C must be a symmetric cone. This includes Lorentz cones, positive semidefinite cones over R, C, H, and the exceptional 3x3 octonionic cone. The authors prove that for any strictly convex cone C (e.g., the cone of positive semidefinite matrices of size >3 over octonions), (C_□, C) fails the LFP. They also show that for any cone C of dimension ≤5, the LFP holds only if C is a direct sum of Lorentz cones. The paper provides explicit counterexamples, such as the cone of 3x3 positive semidefinite matrices over R (which is not symmetric) failing the LFP when paired with C_□. The application to quantum information yields a characterization of cones that allow for a certain type of entanglement witness, linking to the concept of 'Lorentz factorizable' cones.
strengths: Provides a complete characterization for a specific cone (C_□) paired with symmetric cones, which is a non-trivial result.
Uses a clear and rigorous mathematical framework, with well-structured proofs.
Connects abstract cone theory to quantum information, demonstrating practical relevance.
Includes explicit counterexamples and bounds (e.g., dimension ≤5) that clarify the limits of the property.
limitations: The characterization is only for the square-based cone C_□; the general case for arbitrary cones remains open.
The paper does not provide a full classification of all pairs (C1, C2) with the LFP, only negative results for symmetric cases.
The application to quantum information is somewhat brief and could be expanded with more concrete examples or implications.

title: Verifiable And Collusion-Resistant Multi-Party Quantum Private Set Operations
authors: Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Fengxia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threshold private set intersection (TPSI) allows parties to reveal their intersection only when its cardinality reaches a prescribed threshold. Existing quantum TPSI protocols typically rely on a third party (TP) to interpret the final results, which deviates from the cardinality-testing paradigm of TPSI. In this paper, we propose a quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing. Our protocol develops a rotation-based quantum construction in which single-photon sequences are sequentially processed through participant-side data rotations, TP--participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors: TP can complete the final measurement, but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of the outcomes. Based on these hidden measurements, we further realize the threshold decision through an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only \(\mathbf 1[|\bigcap_i X_i|\ge \tau]\) before conditional intersection reconstruction. We prove the correctness and security of the proposed protocol, and further validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations implemented on the IBM platform.
tldr: Proposes a quantum multiparty threshold private set intersection protocol with explicit cardinality testing using rotation-based quantum operations and oblivious linear evaluation.
motivation: Existing quantum TPSI protocols rely on a third party to interpret results, deviating from the cardinality-testing paradigm; this work aims to design a protocol with explicit threshold testing and security against collusion.
method: Uses single-photon sequences processed through participant-side data rotations, TP-participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations to produce hidden-label measurement vectors; threshold decision is realized via OLE-based inner product and a lightweight garbled circuit.
result: Proves correctness and security of the protocol, and validates feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations on IBM platform.
conclusion: The protocol achieves verifiable and collusion-resistant multi-party private set operations with explicit threshold testing, advancing quantum secure multi-party computation.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper proposes a quantum multiparty threshold private set intersection (TPSI) protocol that incorporates explicit cardinality testing, addressing a limitation of existing quantum TPSI protocols that rely on a third party (TP) to interpret final results. The protocol uses a rotation-based quantum construction where single-photon sequences are processed through participant-side data rotations, TP-participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations, producing hidden-label measurement vectors. The TP can perform final measurements but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of outcomes. Threshold decision is achieved via an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only whether the intersection size meets the threshold. The protocol's correctness and security are proven, and feasibility is validated through quantum-circuit simulations on IBM Qiskit.

Novel rotation-based quantum construction using single-photon sequences and hidden-label measurement vectors.
Integration of OLE-based inner product and garbled circuits for threshold decision without revealing intersection size.
Proof of correctness and security against malicious participants and semi-honest TP.
Experimental validation via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM Qiskit platform.

The TP applies masking rotations, and aggregate rotations correlate the sequences. This yields hidden-label measurement vectors that allow the TP to compute inner products via OLE without learning the actual intersection. The threshold decision uses a garbled circuit that outputs only a single bit indicating whether the intersection cardinality exceeds the threshold. The security model assumes semi-honest TP and malicious participants, with security proofs based on quantum indistinguishability and simulation-based arguments. The simulation on Qiskit uses 4 qubits and 3 parties to demonstrate feasibility, though scalability is not explicitly addressed.

title: Composing Quantum Instruments
authors: Robert I. Booth, Dominik Leichtle, Alex Rice, Kim Worrall
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the composition of classically-controlled quantum instruments--the natural quantum analogue of Markov kernels. Classically, Markov kernels compose by integrating one kernel against another. Defining this composition for quantum instruments with continuous outcomes requires an integral of quantum channel-valued functions with respect to a quantum instrument. We construct this integral in the Heisenberg picture using the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension to a von Neumann tensor product. This integral recovers the expected finite formula, preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality, and provides the multiplication for a monad governing the composition of quantum instruments. As an immediate consequence, we identify the category of quantum Markov kernels as the Kleisli category of this monad.
tldr: This paper develops a rigorous framework for composing quantum instruments with continuous outcomes using a monadic approach.
motivation: Classically controlled quantum instruments are the quantum analogue of Markov kernels, but their composition for continuous outcomes requires an integral of channel-valued functions, which was not previously well-defined.
method: The authors construct the integral in the Heisenberg picture using the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension to a von Neumann tensor product, and show it defines a monad whose Kleisli category is the category of quantum Markov kernels.
result: The integral recovers the expected finite formula, preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality, and provides the multiplication for the monad governing composition.
conclusion: This work provides a foundational categorical framework for composing quantum instruments, which is essential for understanding sequential quantum processes and quantum information flow.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework for composing classically-controlled quantum instruments, which are the quantum analogue of classical Markov kernels. The central challenge is defining an integral of quantum channel-valued functions with respect to a quantum instrument when outcomes are continuous. The authors construct this integral in the Heisenberg picture using the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension to a von Neumann tensor product. This integral recovers the expected finite formula, preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality, and provides the multiplication for a monad that governs the composition of quantum instruments. As a direct consequence, the category of quantum Markov kernels is identified as the Kleisli category of this monad. The work is complementary to independent work by Tobias Fritz on the quantum instrument monad in the Schrödinger picture.
key_contributions: Construction of an integral of quantum channel-valued functions with respect to a quantum instrument in the Heisenberg picture using the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension.
Proof that the integral preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality, and recovers the finite-outcome formula.
Definition of a monad on the category of von Neumann algebras whose multiplication is given by this integral, enabling composition of quantum instruments.
Identification of the category of quantum Markov kernels as the Kleisli category of this monad.
Provision of a Heisenberg-picture counterpart to the Schrödinger-picture construction by Tobias Fritz.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is rooted in operator algebra theory and category theory. The authors work in the Heisenberg picture, where quantum instruments are represented as normal completely positive subunital maps from a von Neumann algebra to the tensor product of another von Neumann algebra and the bounded functions on the outcome space. The key technical tool is the Okamura-Ozawa normal extension, which allows embedding the codomain into a von Neumann tensor product, thereby enabling the definition of an integral via a conditional expectation. The integral is defined by first extending the instrument to a normal *-homomorphism, then integrating pointwise, and finally compressing back. The authors verify that this construction satisfies the required properties and yields a monad structure.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is the construction of a monad (T, η, μ) on the category of von Neumann algebras with normal unital *-homomorphisms. The functor T maps a von Neumann algebra A to the space of quantum instruments with outcomes in a standard Borel space Ω, which is itself a von Neumann algebra. The unit η_A sends an element a ∈ A to the instrument that outputs a with certainty. The multiplication μ_A composes two instruments by integrating the first instrument's output channels against the second instrument. The authors show that this integral satisfies the expected properties: it is associative, unital, and preserves normal complete positivity and subunitality. No specific numerical values are given, as the results are structural.
strengths: Rigorous mathematical construction using advanced operator algebra techniques.
Clear connection to category theory via monads, providing a unified framework for composition.
Complementarity to existing Schrödinger-picture work, offering a complete picture.
Potential applications to quantum information theory and quantum probability.
limitations: The construction relies on the Okamura-Ozawa extension, which may be technically heavy for some readers.
The paper does not provide explicit examples or applications beyond the categorical framework.
The assumption of standard Borel outcome spaces may limit generality, though it covers many practical cases.

The use of von Neumann algebras and monads connects to quantum probability and operator algebraic approaches to quantum mechanics. The Heisenberg-picture formulation complements the Schrödinger picture, offering a dual perspective that may be useful for understanding quantum dynamics and control.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations

abstract:

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems with strong correlations, which are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors extend many-body perturbation theory to open quantum systems by combining Keldysh and Lindblad formalisms, introducing diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute nonequilibrium steady states and response functions for driven dissipative quantum systems, capturing both coherent and dissipative dynamics.
conclusion: This work offers a powerful tool for analyzing quantum systems far from equilibrium, with applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information devices.

title: Thermodynamics Of Black Holes, Far From Equilibrium
authors: Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, And Jonathan Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Abhay Ashtekar, Daniel E. Paraizo, and Jonathan Shu

The first law of black hole mechanics has been extended to dynamical horizons so that the law applies to black holes arbitrarily far from equilibrium, a fundamental result that formally shows the thermodynamic description of black holes extends beyond the typical stationary solutions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251405] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Extends the first law of black hole mechanics to dynamical horizons, showing thermodynamic description applies to black holes far from equilibrium.
motivation: To generalize black hole thermodynamics beyond stationary solutions and understand thermodynamic behavior of dynamical black holes.
method: Uses dynamical horizon framework and geometric analysis to derive a first law for non-equilibrium black holes.
result: Establishes a first law for dynamical horizons, linking changes in horizon area to energy and angular momentum fluxes.
conclusion: Black holes can be treated thermodynamically even when far from equilibrium, broadening the scope of black hole thermodynamics.

Reservoir engineering enables unidirectional energy and signal flow. We establish squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities as a guiding principle for exponentially amplifying reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity. Rather than a simple scaling of the coupling, this mechanism strategically…

tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezing-induced symmetry breaking between two cavities can exponentially enhance reservoir-mediated nonreciprocity, providing a new principle for unidirectional signal flow.
motivation: Nonreciprocal devices are essential for quantum information processing, but existing methods face limitations in isolation and bandwidth. The authors aim to develop a more efficient mechanism for enhancing nonreciprocity.
method: They establish a theoretical framework where squeezing in one cavity breaks the symmetry between two coupled cavities, leading to exponentially amplified nonreciprocity in the reservoir-mediated interaction. The model is analyzed using quantum master equations and input-output theory.
result: The squeezing-induced symmetry breaking yields an exponential enhancement of nonreciprocity, far beyond what simple coupling scaling can achieve, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a new guiding principle for engineering nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

A fundamental problem in fault-tolerant quantum computation is the tradeoff between universality and dimensionality, exemplified by the Bravyi-König bound for [MATH]-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. In this Letter, we extend topological Pauli stabilizer codes to a broad class of [MATH]-dimensiona…

tldr: Extends topological stabilizer codes to Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes enabling transversal non-Clifford gates and magic state distillation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires universal gate sets, but transversal gates are limited by the Bravyi-König bound for topological stabilizer codes.
method: Generalizes Pauli stabilizer codes to Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes using higher-form symmetries and gauging, constructing codes with transversal non-Clifford gates.
result: Demonstrates that Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes can circumvent the Bravyi-König bound, allowing transversal T gates and magic state distillation.
conclusion: This work provides a new framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation with improved universality and dimensionality tradeoffs.

authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of multi-site projection operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding based on operator noncommutativity.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index defined via the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: The noncommutative index sharply distinguishes the volume-law and area-law phases, and its critical value matches numerical simulations. The transition is driven by the degree of noncommutativity among measurements.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a universal analytical tool for understanding entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, advancing the theory of quantum information dynamics.

method: The authors implement a higher-order power method on a quantum computer to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: The quantum algorithm is demonstrated on small systems, showing feasibility and potential speedup over classical methods.
conclusion: This work provides a proof-of-principle for quantum-assisted entanglement estimation, which could be useful for benchmarking quantum devices.

abstract:

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…

tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XXZ interactions and a staggered transverse field, showing that the dynamics effectively realize OAT in a collective spin subspace. They analyze the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing.
result: The proposed scheme generates scalable quantum resources, with entanglement and Bell correlations growing with system size, and spin squeezing reaching levels comparable to ideal OAT.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable sources of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing on near-term quantum simulators.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…

tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes to avoid losses, limiting its speed. Accelerating the process violates adiabaticity, causing inefficiency.
method: The authors apply shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) via counter-diabatic driving to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic transitions.
result: The STA-based protocol achieves high-fidelity storage and retrieval in a fraction of the adiabatic time, with efficiency comparable to the adiabatic limit.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-performance quantum memories based on Rydberg EIT, benefiting quantum networks.

The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions remains an open question, particularly for continuous symmetry breaking where zero-temperature Goldstone modes generate long-range correlations. Using large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we investigate the third Rényi …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245145] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the third Rényi negativity across a finite-temperature phase transition in the O(3) universality class using quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: The fate of quantum entanglement at finite-temperature phase transitions, especially with continuous symmetry breaking, is not well understood.
method: Large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the third Rényi negativity for the O(3) model.
result: The third Rényi negativity shows a peak near the critical temperature and obeys scaling laws consistent with the O(3) universality class.
conclusion: Entanglement measures like Rényi negativity can detect finite-temperature phase transitions and exhibit universal scaling behavior.

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics, and the applicability of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism in such systems was unclear.
method: The authors study a dissipative discrete time crystal model and analyze the scaling of spatial defects and transition delay as a function of quench time, using numerical simulations and theoretical scaling arguments.
result: They observe characteristic power-law scaling of defects and transition delay with quench time, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation process.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism universally governs the formation of discrete time crystals in open systems, providing insights into non-equilibrium phase transitions and quantum thermodynamics.

tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurement devices using only trusted state preparation and measurement, without requiring entanglement or additional resources.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, affecting tasks like variational algorithms, error correction, and entanglement distribution.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement device to characterize and purify noisy devices through iterative rounds of measurement and correction, leveraging the concept of quantum state verification.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements, with the required number of rounds scaling polynomially in the desired precision.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and resource-efficient method to mitigate preparation and measurement noise, which is crucial for near-term quantum technologies.

method: The authors use NV centers in diamond to polarize nuclear spins, combined with stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to resolve NMR signals from multiple spin clusters.

conclusion: This work advances the use of NV centers for sensitive NMR detection, with potential applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.

result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.

tldr: This paper investigates gradient scalability in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogate model to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. Understanding when and why gradients vanish is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the gradient scaling of cost functions in VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogate model that approximates the cost landscape, enabling efficient gradient estimation.
result: They show that the Taylor surrogate can predict gradient behavior and identify regimes where barren plateaus are avoided, providing a theoretical framework for scalable VQA training.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of trainability in quantum neural networks and offers a practical tool for designing scalable variational algorithms.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.

tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust differential phase sensing, achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-immune quantum sensor network.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their generation and readout using cavity-mediated interactions.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise, outperforming conventional spin-squeezed states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments, leveraging hybrid quantum systems (atomic ensembles coupled to cavities).

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic code (likely cat code or binomial code) to protect against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary Rydberg array.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a key tool for using circular Rydberg atoms in quantum computing and networking applications.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum algorithms and information theory, and this work aims to delineate where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of computing matrix functions in different parameter regimes using quantum computational complexity theory, likely employing query complexity or circuit complexity measures.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes allow for quantum speedups while others remain classically tractable.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into potential quantum advantages for matrix function problems, guiding future algorithm design and complexity classification.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and coherence times under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the primary cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that operating at cryogenic temperatures and using specific cavity designs can significantly improve stability.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified strategies to further reduce decoherence.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling efficient joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, as demonstrated on experimental data from NV centers.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a scalable and fast approach for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino

tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.

method: The authors develop a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze it using analytical and numerical methods to study kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: They discover blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating how kinetic constraints stabilize these phenomena.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis, Fisher information, and protocols near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality provides a systematic route to achieve Heisenberg-limited sensing and discusses experimental implementations.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation quantum metrology, with potential applications in fundamental physics and technology.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct better ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum control examples.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily available upgrade for quantum control, enhancing performance without requiring additional hardware resources.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times, demonstrating a practical method for erasure conversion in a superconducting qubit platform.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm is efficient and unifies several symmetry-learning tasks, including learning stabilizer groups and beyond.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays

[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.

motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity enhancement are limited by the number of atoms that can be simultaneously coupled to a single cavity mode; multiplexing addresses this scalability bottleneck.
