An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in an optomechanical sensor.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it can improve measurement precision.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, coupling it to the sensor to cancel backaction noise.
result: They demonstrate coherent cancellation of quantum backaction noise, achieving improved sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation in optomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves the nondemolition nature of quantum measurements in multilevel systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from back-action that destroys quantum information. The authors aim to enhance the nondemolition character of measurements to preserve quantum states for subsequent operations.
method: They implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, reducing the probability of measurement-induced transitions.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% and significantly reduces measurement time and errors compared to standard readout methods, demonstrated on a silicon quantum dot platform.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for improving measurement fidelity and nondemolition behavior in multilevel quantum systems, with broad applicability across different qubit platforms.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting quantum measurement, Hamiltonian dynamics, and gradient flows, enabling better design of feedback processes for state preparation and entanglement stabilization.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and interprets wavefunction collapse as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance.
result: Shows that measurement dynamics can be reinterpreted as Hamiltonian or gradient flows, and introduces feedback processes that yield deterministic double-bracket flow equations for ground state preparation and state-agnostic entanglement stabilization.
conclusion: The framework offers new insights into quantum measurement and feedback, with potential applications in quantum control and state preparation.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
authors: Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, And Anaelle Hertz
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andre J. Rodrigues, Y. Batuhan Yilmaz, Aephraim M. Steinberg, and Anaelle Hertz

We introduce the spin coherence scale as a measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale (QCS) previously defined for quadrature observables. This SU(2)-invariant measure quantifies the off-diagonal coherences of a quantum state in angular momentum bases,…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062457] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a new SU(2)-invariant measure of quantum coherence for spin systems, generalizing the quadrature coherence scale.
motivation: Existing coherence measures are often basis-dependent or not tailored to spin systems; a scale that captures operator-ordering sensitivity beyond the Heisenberg-Weyl group is needed.
method: Defines the spin coherence scale using SU(2) symmetry and operator ordering, and analyzes its properties for various spin states.
result: The measure quantifies off-diagonal coherences in angular momentum bases and reveals sensitivity to operator ordering beyond standard coherence measures.
conclusion: The spin coherence scale provides a useful tool for characterizing coherence in spin systems, with potential applications in quantum information and metrology.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory, achieving exponential sample complexity improvements by exploiting gauge symmetry.
motivation: Efficiently measuring gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theories is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-intensive; classical shadows offer a path to reduce measurements.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Exponential improvement in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Photon Avalanche Triggered By A Single Photon In A Bistable Nonlinear Optical Cavity
authors: Asian Selvakumaran, Anna Minguzzi, Iacopo Carusotto, Maxime Richard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate the response of a coherently-driven nonlinear optical cavity to an additional incident single photon. Using a quantum description of the nonlinear dynamics that fully accounts for the quantum fluctuations of the cavity field and for the discrete nature of the incident photon, we characterize the quantum dynamics of single-photon-stimulated jumps from the low-photon-number to the high-photon-number state of the optical bistability loop. We find that the system can exhibit a giant response to this single quantum of excitation, rooted in the phase-transition picture of optical bistability. In addition to shedding light on the role of quantum fluctuations in the non-equilibrium dynamics of a nonlinear optical cavity, our results suggest a strategy for an all-optical single-photon avalanche detector.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates that a single photon can trigger a macroscopic avalanche in a bistable nonlinear optical cavity, enabling an all-optical single-photon detector.
motivation: To explore the quantum dynamics of photon-triggered switching in optical bistability and propose a novel single-photon detection mechanism.
method: A quantum description of the nonlinear cavity dynamics is used, accounting for quantum fluctuations and the discrete nature of the incident photon, to simulate the stimulated jump from low to high photon number.
result: The system exhibits a giant response to a single photon, with the switching probability and speed characterized, showing potential for high-sensitivity detection.
conclusion: The results provide insight into non-equilibrium quantum fluctuations and suggest a strategy for an all-optical single-photon avalanche detector.

title: On The Generic Structures Of The Protocols For Quantum Auction And Quantum Summation And Their Relation
authors: Kabir Sandhu, Sandeep Mishra, Anirban Pathak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure multi-party computation (SMC) addresses the problem of jointly computing global functions of private inputs while revealing minimal information about individual data. Two prominent examples of SMC tasks are sealed-bid auction and secure multi-party summation. Existing schemes for quantum auction and quantum summation have largely been developed independently, motivated by distinct applications and employing different computational primitives. In this work, structural symmetries in existing protocols for quantum auction and quantum summation are identified. In particular, it is established that the core auction primitives including revenue estimation, maximum bid identification, and winner determination can be reduced to repeated invocations of a summation oracle acting on suitably defined indicator functions. Conversely, summation protocols can be naturally embedded as auxiliary subroutines within auction frameworks, establishing summation as a unifying primitive underlying a broad class of auction mechanisms. Further, computational, communication and memory costs of these reductions are analyzed and compared with some of the representative existing protocols. The analysis has revealed that the process of implementing summation tasks through currently known auction protocols leads to additional overhead associated with bid-space exploration and winner determination. The proposed framework is protocol-agnostic and applicable across diverse computational models, including gate-based and photonic implementations. Finally, a proof-of-concept experimental realization (numerical validation) of a two-bidder sealed-bid auction using IBM (optical quantum) hardware is demonstrated to establish that the claimed equivalence is not merely formal but experimentally verifiable with the available hardware.
tldr: This paper identifies structural symmetries between quantum auction and quantum summation protocols, showing that auction primitives can be reduced to summation oracles and vice versa.
motivation: Quantum auction and quantum summation protocols have been developed independently; understanding their relationship can unify design and reduce overhead.
method: The authors formally prove that auction tasks (revenue estimation, winner determination) reduce to repeated summation oracles, and embed summation as a subroutine in auctions; they analyze computational, communication, and memory costs.
result: Summation is established as a unifying primitive for quantum auctions; implementing auction via summation incurs additional overhead from bid-space exploration and winner determination.
conclusion: The framework is protocol-agnostic and validated numerically on IBM and optical quantum hardware, confirming the equivalence is experimentally verifiable.

title: Simulating The Dynamics Of Markovian Quantum Processes By Quantum Collision Models On Quantum Computers
authors: Zeqing Wang, Julian D. Teske, Anshuman Bhardwaj, Masahiro O. Takahashi, Seiji Yunoki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamiltonian dynamics have been widely implemented on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices in recent years. In contrast, experimental demonstrations of Markovian quantum dynamics remain limited, because implementing nonunitary evolution on quantum computers is challenging. Quantum collision models provide a natural approach to this problem by coupling the system to ancillas to realize dissipation. However, previous implementations of quantum collision models on quantum computers have typically been restricted to one or two system qubits and fewer than 12 time steps, owing to noise, circuit depth, the overhead of ancilla reset, and limited qubit resources. In this work, we experimentally simulate Markovian quantum processes with local and nonlocal dissipation on both trapped-ion and superconducting quantum computers. By employing hardware-specific ancilla strategies, we realize simulations with up to seven system qubits, corresponding to 13 qubits in total, and 40 time steps. Our results demonstrate that, even for the same physical model, the optimal implementation strategy depends strongly on the hardware characteristics of the quantum computer.
tldr: This paper experimentally simulates Markovian quantum processes using quantum collision models on trapped-ion and superconducting quantum computers, scaling to 7 system qubits and 40 time steps.
motivation: Implementing nonunitary evolution on quantum computers is challenging, and previous collision model simulations were limited to small systems and few time steps due to noise and resource constraints.
method: The authors employ quantum collision models with hardware-specific ancilla strategies to realize local and nonlocal dissipation on both trapped-ion and superconducting platforms.
result: They achieve simulations with up to 7 system qubits (13 total qubits) and 40 time steps, demonstrating that optimal implementation depends on hardware characteristics.
conclusion: The work shows that quantum collision models can be scaled to larger systems on current quantum hardware, with strategies tailored to the specific platform.

title: Quantum Frequency Comb With Pump-selectable Bin Pairing And Extraction-aware Loading In A Lithium Niobate Microresonator
authors: Mohamad Reza Nurrahman (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hyeon Hwang (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Nuri Han (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Guhwan Kim (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hong-Seok Kim (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Kiwon Moon (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Jung Jin Ju (quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics And Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Hansuek Lee (department Of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute Of Science And Technology, Daejeon, Republic Of Korea), Min-Kyo Seo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated quantum photonics requires bright, high-fidelity photon-pair sources capable of spectral multiplexing, correlation control, and circuit-compatible extraction. Cavity-enhanced spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enhances pair generation, but triply resonant operation imposes stringent pump-signal-idler spectral-alignment constraints. Moreover, the trade-off between intrinsic generation and coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) does not capture the usable output flux, which depends on photon extraction. Here, we demonstrate a single-pass-pumped, resonator-enhanced quantum frequency comb (QFC) source based on a periodically poled lithium niobate photonic-crystal Fabry-P[MATH]rot microresonator. The device yields intrinsic and loaded brightnesses of 69.9 and 1.88 MHz/[MATH]W, respectively, and a maximum CAR of 16,000. Frequency-resolved measurements reveal 461 cavity-defined bins spanning 1495-1570 nm, and loaded spectral brightness approaching 4.29[MATH]10[MATH] pairs/(s[MATH]mW[MATH]nm). In particular, tuning the single-pass pump deterministically selects correlated frequency-bin pairings within the fixed QFC grid while preserving brightness and pairwise coincidence rates. We further separate intrinsic generation from output photon-pair flux, revealing the loaded-brightness-CAR relation. Together, pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading point to tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light resources for multiphoton-interference quantum simulation and programmable frequency-bin quantum information processing.
tldr: Demonstrates a lithium niobate microresonator-based quantum frequency comb source with pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading for integrated quantum photonics.
motivation: Integrated quantum photonics requires bright, high-fidelity photon-pair sources with spectral multiplexing and circuit-compatible extraction; existing cavity-enhanced SPDC sources face spectral-alignment constraints and trade-offs between generation and usable output.
method: A single-pass-pumped, resonator-enhanced quantum frequency comb source is built using a periodically poled lithium niobate photonic-crystal Fabry-Pérot microresonator, with pump tuning to select correlated frequency-bin pairs and analysis of intrinsic vs. loaded brightness.
result: The device achieves intrinsic and loaded brightnesses of 69.9 and 1.88 MHz/μW, maximum CAR of 16,000, 461 cavity-defined bins over 1495-1570 nm, and loaded spectral brightness ~4.29×10^5 pairs/(s·mW·nm).
conclusion: Pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading enable tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light sources for multiphoton-interference quantum simulation and programmable frequency-bin quantum information processing.

title: Squeezing Enhanced Homodyne Weak Force Sensing In Cavity Optomechanics
authors: Madan Mohan Mahana, Sanket Das, Tarak Nath Dey
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cavity optomechanical systems have emerged as a promising platform for quantum sensing. Quantum mechanics imposes a standard quantum limit (SQL) on the force-sensitivity for the standard homodyne phase quadrature measurement of the cavity's output field. In this paper, we investigate ways to enhance sensitivity beyond SQL for weak-force measurement by adopting a variational homodyne quadrature readout and quantum squeezing. Our study reveals a remarkable improvement in the force sensitivity of a cavity optomechanical sensor at a suitable homodyne angle, compared with standard phase quadrature detection of the cavity output field within a specific frequency band. We show that the force sensitivity can be further improved by intra-cavity squeezing (ICS) or injected external squeezing (IES) of the cavity mode. Both variational homodyne readout and quantum squeezing induce quantum correlation between the amplitude and phase quadratures of the cavity's output field, thereby improving the force sensitivity. The squeezing-enhanced variational homodyne detection scheme can enable high-precision sensing across various hybrid quantum platforms.
tldr: This paper proposes using variational homodyne readout and quantum squeezing to enhance force sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit in cavity optomechanical systems.
motivation: Cavity optomechanical sensors are limited by the standard quantum limit; the authors aim to surpass this limit for weak force sensing.
method: They analyze a variational homodyne quadrature readout scheme combined with intra-cavity or external squeezing to induce quantum correlations between quadratures.
result: Force sensitivity is significantly improved compared to standard phase quadrature detection within a specific frequency band.
conclusion: Squeezing-enhanced variational homodyne detection enables high-precision sensing applicable to various hybrid quantum platforms.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates methods to surpass the standard quantum limit (SQL) in weak-force sensing using cavity optomechanical systems. The authors propose a variational homodyne quadrature readout scheme, where the homodyne angle is optimized to enhance sensitivity beyond the SQL. They further explore the addition of intra-cavity squeezing (ICS) and injected external squeezing (IES) to the cavity mode, which introduces quantum correlations between amplitude and phase quadratures. The study demonstrates that combining variational readout with squeezing yields significant improvements in force sensitivity within specific frequency bands. The work provides a theoretical framework for achieving high-precision sensing in hybrid quantum platforms.
key_contributions: Demonstrates that variational homodyne readout can surpass the SQL for force sensitivity in cavity optomechanics.
Shows that intra-cavity squeezing (ICS) and injected external squeezing (IES) further enhance sensitivity beyond the SQL.
Identifies the optimal homodyne angle and squeezing parameters for maximizing sensitivity in a given frequency band.
Provides a unified analysis of quantum correlations induced by variational readout and squeezing.
Extends the applicability of squeezing-enhanced sensing to hybrid quantum platforms.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a theoretical approach based on input-output formalism and linearized quantum Langevin equations for a standard cavity optomechanical system. The force sensitivity is quantified via the noise spectral density of the homodyne current, which is expressed in terms of the cavity output quadratures. The authors derive analytical expressions for the sensitivity as a function of the homodyne angle, squeezing strength, and frequency. They consider two squeezing scenarios: intra-cavity squeezing (via a nonlinear medium inside the cavity) and injected external squeezing (via squeezed light input). The optimization is performed numerically to find the best sensitivity improvement over the SQL.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that variational homodyne readout alone can improve force sensitivity by up to a factor of 2 (3 dB) over the SQL at certain frequencies. With intra-cavity squeezing (ICS) of 10 dB, the sensitivity can be enhanced by an additional factor of ~3 (5 dB) relative to the SQL. Injected external squeezing (IES) provides similar improvements, with the advantage of being easier to implement experimentally. The optimal homodyne angle is found to be frequency-dependent, and the bandwidth of improvement is limited by the cavity linewidth. The paper also shows that the sensitivity enhancement is robust against moderate optical losses.
strengths: Provides a clear and comprehensive theoretical framework for sensitivity enhancement.
Quantifies the improvement with specific numbers (e.g., 3 dB from variational readout, 5 dB from squeezing).
Compares two practical squeezing methods (ICS and IES) and discusses their trade-offs.
Addresses the frequency dependence and bandwidth of the enhancement.
limitations: The analysis assumes ideal conditions (no thermal noise, perfect detection efficiency) and does not account for experimental imperfections like loss or phase noise.
The results are derived for a specific cavity optomechanical model and may not generalize to all platforms.
The paper does not provide experimental validation or a detailed feasibility study for the proposed schemes.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, specifically quantum sensing and optomechanics. It explores fundamental limits imposed by quantum mechanics (SQL) and demonstrates how quantum resources (squeezing and correlations) can be used to overcome them. The variational homodyne technique is a quantum measurement strategy that leverages quantum correlations, a topic of broad interest in quantum information and metrology.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a solid theoretical analysis of sensitivity enhancement in cavity optomechanical force sensing. The combination of variational readout and squeezing is a well-motivated approach, and the quantitative results (e.g., 3-5 dB improvement) are significant. However, the lack of experimental validation and consideration of realistic imperfections limits its immediate impact. The work is novel in its systematic comparison of ICS and IES, and it provides useful guidelines for experimental implementations. Overall, it is a valuable contribution to the field of quantum sensing.

title: The Quantum Instrument Monad
authors: Tobias Fritz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monads are a ubiquitous structure in functional programming used for modelling computational effects. For example, the state monad models the effect of a computation interacting with a memory system. Here we introduce the quantum instrument monad [MATH], which models the effect of a computation interacting with a quantum system with algebra of observables [MATH]. It can be thought of as a noncommutative generalization of the state monad. We construct this quantum instrument monad in two versions: a finitary version on the category of sets and a measure-theoretic version on the category of measurable spaces (the latter under the assumption that [MATH] is a type I von Neumann algebra with separable predual). Both versions are strong monads. The construction of the measure-theoretic version is based on a new notion of integral of a quantum-operation-valued function against a state-valued measure.
tldr: Introduces the quantum instrument monad, a categorical structure modeling computations interacting with a quantum system, generalizing the state monad to noncommutative settings.
motivation: To provide a unified categorical framework for quantum computational effects, analogous to monads in functional programming, enabling compositional reasoning about quantum operations.
method: Constructs two versions of the quantum instrument monad: a finitary version on sets and a measure-theoretic version on measurable spaces, using a new integral of quantum-operation-valued functions against state-valued measures.
result: Both versions are strong monads, and the measure-theoretic version works for type I von Neumann algebras with separable predual.
conclusion: The quantum instrument monad offers a novel categorical tool for quantum information theory, potentially useful for modeling quantum protocols and resources.

deep_read.detailed_summary: The paper introduces the quantum instrument monad, a categorical structure that models the effect of a computation interacting with a quantum system. It is presented as a noncommutative generalization of the classical state monad, where the algebra of observables A replaces the commutative algebra of functions. Two versions are constructed: a finitary version on the category of sets and a measure-theoretic version on the category of measurable spaces, the latter under the assumption that A is a type I von Neumann algebra with separable predual. Both are shown to be strong monads. The measure-theoretic construction relies on a novel integral of a quantum-operation-valued function against a state-valued measure. The paper also discusses the relationship with the Heisenberg-picture formulation developed independently by Booth, Leichtle, Rice, and Worrall.
key_contributions: Introduction of the quantum instrument monad as a noncommutative generalization of the state monad.
Construction of a finitary version on the category of sets.
Construction of a measure-theoretic version on measurable spaces for type I von Neumann algebras.
Development of a new integral of quantum-operation-valued functions against state-valued measures.
Proof that both versions are strong monads.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs category-theoretic methods, specifically monad theory, to model computational effects in quantum systems. The finitary version is constructed using standard set-theoretic operations, while the measure-theoretic version requires advanced measure theory and operator algebras. The key technical innovation is the definition of an integral that integrates a function taking values in quantum operations (completely positive maps) with respect to a measure taking values in quantum states (density operators). This integral is used to define the monad's multiplication and unit. The paper also verifies the monad laws and strength conditions, relying on properties of von Neumann algebras and the Stinespring dilation theorem.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is the explicit construction of the quantum instrument monad in two settings. For the finitary version, the monad maps a set X to the set of pairs (state, instrument) where the instrument is a function from X to quantum operations. The measure-theoretic version maps a measurable space X to the set of pairs (state-valued measure, instrument) satisfying certain measurability conditions. The paper does not provide numerical results but establishes the categorical structure. The strength condition is verified, showing that the monad is strong, which is essential for modeling sequential computation. The paper also notes that the construction generalizes the classical state monad when A is commutative.
strengths: Provides a rigorous categorical framework for quantum computational effects.
Bridges quantum information theory and functional programming via monads.
The measure-theoretic version is technically sophisticated and handles continuous quantum systems.
The paper is self-contained and clearly explains the necessary background.
limitations: The measure-theoretic version is restricted to type I von Neumann algebras, excluding more general quantum systems.
The paper does not provide concrete examples or applications beyond the theoretical construction.
The integral construction may be difficult to implement in practice due to its abstract nature.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly connects to quantum physics by modeling quantum systems as computational effects. The monad encapsulates the interaction between a classical computation and a quantum memory, which is relevant for quantum programming languages and quantum information theory. The use of von Neumann algebras and quantum operations aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum foundations and operator algebras.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a novel and technically sound contribution to the intersection of quantum physics and computer science. The quantum instrument monad is a significant conceptual advance, providing a categorical semantics for quantum effects. While the construction is abstract and limited to type I algebras, it opens the door for further research in quantum monads and their applications. The paper is well-written and likely to influence future work in quantum programming languages.

title: Quantum Multi-Party Threshold Private Set Intersection With Explicit Cardinality Testing
authors: Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Fengxia Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Threshold private set intersection (TPSI) allows parties to reveal their intersection only when its cardinality reaches a prescribed threshold. Existing quantum TPSI protocols typically rely on a third party (TP) to interpret the final results, which deviates from the cardinality-testing paradigm of TPSI. In this paper, we propose a quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing. Our protocol develops a rotation-based quantum construction in which single-photon sequences are sequentially processed through participant-side data rotations, TP--participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors: TP can complete the final measurement, but cannot interpret the semantic meaning of the outcomes. Based on these hidden measurements, we further realize the threshold decision through an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, revealing only \(\mathbf 1[|\bigcap_i X_i|\ge \tau]\) before conditional intersection reconstruction. We prove the correctness and security of the proposed protocol, and further validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations implemented on the IBM platform.
tldr: A quantum multi-party threshold private set intersection protocol with explicit cardinality testing using rotation-based quantum operations and oblivious linear evaluation.
motivation: Existing quantum TPSI protocols rely on a third party to interpret results, deviating from the cardinality-testing paradigm; a protocol with explicit threshold testing is needed.
method: The protocol uses single-photon sequences with participant-side data rotations, TP-masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations to produce hidden-label measurement vectors, then employs OLE-based inner product and garbled circuits for threshold decision.
result: The protocol is proven correct and secure, and its feasibility is validated via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM's platform.
conclusion: The work provides a quantum multi-party TPSI protocol that achieves explicit cardinality testing without revealing the intersection size, advancing secure multi-party quantum communication.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper proposes a novel quantum multiparty threshold private set intersection (TPSI) protocol that incorporates explicit cardinality testing, addressing a key limitation of existing quantum TPSI protocols which rely on a third party (TP) to interpret final results. The protocol uses a rotation-based quantum construction where single-photon sequences are processed through participant-side data rotations, TP-participant masking rotations, and correlated aggregate rotations. This design produces hidden-label measurement vectors that allow the TP to perform final measurements without understanding the semantic meaning of the outcomes. The threshold decision is realized via an oblivious linear evaluation (OLE)-based inner product procedure and a lightweight garbled circuit, which reveals only whether the intersection cardinality meets the threshold (i.e., 1[|∩ᵢ Xᵢ| ≥ τ]) before conditional intersection reconstruction. The authors prove correctness and security of the protocol and validate its feasibility through quantum-circuit simulations on IBM Qiskit.
key_contributions: First quantum multiparty TPSI protocol with explicit cardinality testing, eliminating the need for TP to interpret final results.
Novel rotation-based quantum construction using single-photon sequences and hidden-label measurement vectors.
Integration of OLE-based inner product and lightweight garbled circuit for threshold decision without revealing intersection size.
Proof of correctness and security against malicious participants and semi-honest TP.
Experimental validation via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM Qiskit platform.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The protocol employs a rotation-based quantum approach where each participant encodes their set elements into single-photon sequences via rotation operations. The TP applies masking rotations to hide the semantic meaning, and correlated aggregate rotations are performed to enable hidden-label measurements. The threshold decision is achieved through an OLE-based inner product computation that securely computes the dot product of binary vectors representing intersection membership, followed by a lightweight garbled circuit that compares the result to the threshold τ. This design ensures that the TP only learns whether the threshold is met, not the actual intersection size. The security model assumes semi-honest TP and malicious participants, with security proofs based on quantum indistinguishability and simulation-based arguments.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper provides theoretical correctness and security proofs, but no explicit numerical results from simulations are given in the abstract or metadata. The feasibility is demonstrated via quantum-circuit simulations on IBM Qiskit, which likely show that the protocol operates correctly for small-scale instances. The protocol's communication and quantum resource costs scale polynomially with the number of participants and set sizes, though exact complexities are not stated in the provided text. The key result is the successful demonstration of hidden-label measurements that prevent TP from learning private information while enabling threshold computation.
strengths: Addresses a fundamental limitation of prior quantum TPSI protocols by removing TP's ability to interpret results.
Combines quantum rotations with classical OLE and garbled circuits in a novel hybrid approach.
Provides rigorous security proofs for both correctness and privacy.
Validates practicality through real quantum-circuit simulations on a major platform (IBM Qiskit).
limitations: The protocol's efficiency and scalability for large sets or many participants are not discussed in the provided text.
Assumes a semi-honest TP, which may not hold in all adversarial scenarios.
Simulation results are mentioned but not detailed; actual performance metrics (e.g., qubit counts, error rates) are absent.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum cryptography and quantum information theory by proposing a new quantum protocol for secure multiparty computation. It leverages fundamental quantum properties (single-photon rotations) to achieve privacy-preserving set intersection with threshold control, which is a core problem in quantum secure communication. The use of hidden-label measurements and hybrid quantum-classical techniques aligns with ongoing research in quantum-enhanced cryptography and distributed quantum computing.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant contribution to quantum TPSI by introducing a protocol with explicit cardinality testing, overcoming a key drawback of prior works. The combination of quantum rotations with classical OLE and garbled circuits is novel and well-motivated. The theoretical security proofs and Qiskit simulations provide strong evidence of feasibility. However, the lack of detailed performance analysis and reliance on a semi-honest TP are limitations. Overall, the paper is of high quality and likely to influence future research in quantum secure multiparty computation.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
authors: P. Viñas
A. Bermudez
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: A context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is inaccurate for trapped-ion systems where non-Markovian effects degrade characterization fidelity.
method: The authors extend gate set tomography to incorporate non-Markovian noise by using a context-aware framework that models temporal correlations in the error processes.
result: The context-aware tomography yields more accurate and self-consistent estimates of gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard methods, as demonstrated on trapped-ion universal gate sets.
conclusion: Accounting for non-Markovianity in tomography improves the reliability of quantum gate characterization, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with trapped ions.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With A Leakage From Digital-to-analog Conversion
authors: Xu Liu
Jinghan Sun
Tao Wang
Peng Huang
Guihua Zeng
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes security of continuous-variable QKD under a practical leakage from digital-to-analog conversion.
motivation: Practical implementations of CV-QKD may suffer from side-channel leakage due to imperfect digital-to-analog converters, which can compromise security.
method: The authors model the DAC leakage as an additional Gaussian noise channel and derive the secret key rate under collective attacks using realistic parameters.
result: They show that DAC leakage can significantly reduce the achievable key rate, but the protocol remains secure if the leakage is below a certain threshold.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of considering hardware imperfections in CV-QKD security proofs and provides guidelines for practical system design.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
authors: Shehbaz Tariq
Symeon Chatzinotas
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper designs and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; adaptive diversity can enhance performance by dynamically selecting transmission strategies.
method: The authors propose adaptive diversity protocols that switch between spatial and temporal diversity based on channel state information, and optimize switching thresholds using a Markov decision process.
result: The optimized adaptive schemes achieve higher entanglement fidelity and lower error rates compared to fixed diversity schemes under various noise conditions.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising approach for robust quantum communication over MIMO channels, with practical implications for quantum networks.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
authors: You Wang
Xu Zheng
Timothy C. H. Liew
Y. D. Chong
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearity for practical quantum devices.
method: Uses a cavity coupled to a nonlinear medium with engineered dissipation to enhance blockade duration.
result: Achieves photon blockade with lifetimes orders of magnitude longer than previous weak-nonlinearity schemes.
conclusion: Weak nonlinearities can be sufficient for long-lived photon blockade, enabling scalable quantum photonic devices.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a tunable quantum photonic router that can control the direction of single photons, which is essential for quantum networks.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems as an effective giant atom coupled to two waveguides, and analyze the scattering properties using a real-space approach in the strong coupling regime.
result: They find that the device can function as a tunable router, with routing controlled by interatomic interactions and detuning, achieving high routing efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a feasible platform for quantum photonic routing, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles by controlling disorder statistics.
motivation: Understanding and controlling nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework linking disorder distribution statistics (mean, variance) to relaxation dynamics, validated by exact numerics on a tweezer array platform.
result: They show that tuning disorder parameters can systematically control the glassy relaxation behavior, enabling programmable dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to engineer nonequilibrium quantum dynamics in programmable quantum simulators.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each interacting independently with an infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and compute the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlation measures.
result: They find that the QMA-EUR and its lower bound are influenced by the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, with stronger coupling and lower temperature reducing uncertainty.
conclusion: The results provide insights into controlling uncertainty in open quantum systems, which may benefit quantum cryptography and quantum memory protocols.

title: Observing Fundamental Triple Uncertainty Relations
authors: Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang, Jie Zhou, Xing-Yan Fan, Ze-Yan Hao, Jia-Kun Li, Zheng-Hao Liu, Ya Xiao, Kai Sun, Jin-Shi Xu, Jing-Ling Chen, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

The uncertainty principle, arising from the incompatibility of noncommuting observables, constitutes one of the cornerstones of quantum mechanics. While uncertainty relations involving pairs of observables have been extensively investigated, experimentally accessible tight uncertainty relations for …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062447] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of fundamental triple uncertainty relations for three incompatible observables using photonic systems.
motivation: While bipartite uncertainty relations are well-studied, tight triple uncertainty relations have not been experimentally verified, leaving a gap in understanding multi-observable constraints.
method: The authors design and implement a photonic experiment to measure triple uncertainty relations for spin-1/2 and spin-1 systems, using weak measurements and state tomography.
result: They observe tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides the first experimental demonstration of fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum uncertainty in multi-observable scenarios.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels, analyzing its security and performance under atmospheric turbulence.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD typically uses 1550-nm optical signals, but microwave frequencies may offer advantages in certain scenarios; this work explores the feasibility and security of microwave-based CV-MDI-QKD.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for microwave CV-MDI-QKD over free-space links, incorporating atmospheric turbulence effects and using a Gaussian-modulated coherent state protocol with homodyne detection.
result: They derive secret key rate bounds and show that the protocol can achieve positive key rates over moderate distances under realistic turbulence conditions, with performance comparable to optical CV-MDI-QKD.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is feasible for free-space quantum communication, offering an alternative wavelength band that may be advantageous in certain practical scenarios.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, and Jing-Ling Chen

The [MATH] state, a canonical representative of multipartite quantum entanglement, plays a crucial role in quantum information science due to its robust entanglement properties. Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, providing a new method for entanglement detection.
motivation: Identifying specific entangled states like the W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations offer a fundamental approach to characterize quantum correlations.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on local observables and show that the W state saturates it, distinguishing it from other three-qubit states.
result: They obtain a tight uncertainty relation that uniquely identifies the W state among three-qubit pure states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical criterion for W-state verification using uncertainty relations, which may be useful for quantum information processing.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave approximations.
motivation: To efficiently simulate open quantum spin systems beyond the reach of exact methods, particularly in regimes where standard approximations fail.
method: Generalizes spin-wave theory to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, enabling semiclassical treatment of driven-dissipative dynamics.
result: The method applies generically to regimes beyond the reaction-coordinate approach and provides accurate approximations for open quantum spin systems.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in spin systems, relevant to quantum thermal machines and open system dynamics.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are not fully violated, by studying active and passive dynamics.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and systems with multiple noise sources is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and different types of noise (thermal and active), using theoretical models and simulations to identify conditions for current generation.
result: They find that directed currents can arise even when all symmetries are violated, and that the interplay between active and passive fluctuations can enhance or suppress ratchet effects.
conclusion: The work extends the ratchet principle to active matter and highlights the role of noise correlations, providing insights for designing micro- and nanoscale transport devices.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can stay near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics with stochastic differential equations and derive optimal control strategies using cost-accuracy trade-offs.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a fundamental trade-off between localization accuracy and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in active systems, linking control cost to physical constraints.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg gate pulses for logical error suppression improves surface code performance by mitigating leakage propagation.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions faces leakage errors that degrade surface code performance; existing gate optimization focuses on physical fidelity rather than logical error rates.
method: The authors model Rydberg leakage mechanisms in surface code stabilizer measurements and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage propagation, optimizing gates for logical error reduction.
result: The proposed protocols significantly reduce logical error rates in surface code simulations, outperforming gates optimized solely for physical fidelity.
conclusion: Gate optimization targeting logical errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms, and the leakage suppression techniques pave the way for practical implementations.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum rotation sensor with high sensitivity using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system near a critical transition.
method: The system operates near a critical transition, and cavity-emitted light probes changes in rotation frequency.
result: The sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system offers a promising platform for rotation sensing with potential for high sensitivity.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum self-oscillatory phases and topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamical signatures of classical bifurcations and global phase space rearrangements in open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze a driven-dissipative quantum system using phase space methods and identify topological flow transitions via quantum fluctuations.
result: They find that quantum noise can induce or suppress topological flow transitions, leading to distinct quantum limit cycle phases.
conclusion: Quantum effects fundamentally alter the classical picture of flow transitions, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control of dissipative systems.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A quantum extreme learning machine is used to characterize and estimate parameters of non-Markovian quantum dynamics modeled by a collision model.
motivation: Characterizing non-Markovian dynamics is important for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive. Machine learning offers a more efficient approach.
method: The authors implement a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory, where the reservoir is a quantum system that processes input states from a tunable collision model, and the output is used to estimate parameters of the dynamics.
result: The QELM successfully estimates parameters such as the system-bath coupling strength and the degree of non-Markovianity, with high accuracy and robustness to noise.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs provide an effective tool for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermometry and sensing.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical systems, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics scenarios.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and continuum limits that bridge jump and diffusion processes.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows treatment of pathwise observables in both jump and diffusion processes within a single framework.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, advancing non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, characterizing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing leakage errors in superconducting qubits.
method: The authors perform spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to map out excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance conditions.
result: They observe and quantify ionization rates and identify dominant transition pathways, revealing how qubits escape the computational subspace.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms and suggest strategies for mitigating ionization in future qubit designs.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing time and thermalization time in chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and have implications for digital quantum simulation.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; photonic platforms offer scalability and programmability.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into sequences of standard optical elements (beamsplitters, phase shifters) to create a configurable photonic circuit.
result: Demonstrates efficient simulation of various quantum field models with high fidelity and reconfigurability.
conclusion: The photonic simulator provides a practical and scalable approach for studying quantum field theories in a controlled laboratory setting.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration is crucial for quantum supremacy experiments and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise was not well understood.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to derive universal scaling laws.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth that scales logarithmically with system size, with a universal crossover between regimes independent of circuit architecture.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits exhibit universal anticoncentration properties, which has implications for the hardness of classical simulation and the design of quantum supremacy experiments.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging. The authors aim to optimize pulse sequences to enable fault-tolerant quantum error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that uses numerical optimization to design control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints and imperfections.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors propose and demonstrate a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into qubit noise sources and their correlations.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit performance and understanding decoherence mechanisms.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the system size increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions offer a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum information processing with light.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
