tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the origin of magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model narrow-band system using theoretical methods to compare the stability of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states.
result: They find that quantum geometry and band dispersion jointly determine the preferred magnetic ordering.
conclusion: The work provides insights into magnetism in narrow-band systems but is not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism in condensed matter systems.
motivation: The antiferroaxial state is an important ferroic order, and the authors aim to show that it can induce altermagnetism, providing a new multiferroic mechanism.
method: The authors develop a microscopic theory linking antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions to altermagnetism, likely using symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations.
result: They demonstrate that antiferroaxial altermagnetism is broadly prevalent and generic in condensed matter systems.
conclusion: This work identifies a new class of multiferroic materials with coupled antiferroaxial and altermagnetic orders.

title: Flexible Gravitational-Wave Parameter Estimation With Transformers
authors: Annalena Kofler, Maximilian Dax, Stephen R. Green, Jonas Wildberger, Nihar Gupte, Jakob H. Macke, Jonathan Gair, Alessandra Buonanno, And Bernhard Schölkopf

method: The author develops an octant geometric framework that maps three-state optical modes onto the positive surface of a sphere spanned by a torus, covering the entire state space except for isolated singularities.
result: The parametrization covers all higher-order optical modes except where a mode amplitude vanishes, offering a complete geometric representation.
conclusion: This geometric framework may be useful for structured light applications but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: They identify multiple coexisting phases in real space and characterize their structures and proximity effects.

conclusion: The plane-wave AFQMC implementation is a viable and accurate approach for computing lattice constants, with potential for broader application in condensed matter physics.

method: The authors extend downfolding techniques to include arbitrary-range electron-phonon coupling, deriving effective Hamiltonians from first-principles calculations.
result: They demonstrate that long-range coupling significantly affects the low-energy subspace and can be systematically included in downfolding.
conclusion: The method provides a more complete framework for modeling electron-phonon interactions in materials, improving accuracy for systems where long-range coupling is important.

conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into stochastic search in heterogeneous media, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three complementary real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how each technique provides unique information about disorder and how combining them yields a more comprehensive understanding.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, are powerful tools for characterizing atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: To understand stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, which require knowledge of nuclear reactions at very low energies that are difficult to measure directly.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions.
result: Provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of low-energy nuclear reaction theory and experimental methods.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar processes and element formation.

title: Causality Of Ultrafast Photoionization From Argon 3 S Usin...
authors: Rezvan Tahouri And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract: We study real-time photoionization flux at the Amusia–Cooper minimum (ACM) in argon using ab initio simulations with the relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) method in length (LG) and velocity (VG) gauges. A simple analytical model is used to interpret the results, and to construct Wigner delays and Wigner distributions for both gauges and relativistic channels of the photoelectron ( with and ). The two gauges are found to produce qualitatively different ionization dynamics, with LG having positive and VG having negative Wigner delays. The advancement of several femtoseconds, found for Wigner delays in VG, raises some concern for causality when atoms are ionized by attosecond pulses that are shorter than the absolute value of the Wigner delay. Reassuringly, numerical simulations of wave packets with RTDCIS show that the electrons behave in a causal way in both gauges. Weighted delays that take into account the temporal window of excitation (or the bandwidth of the pulses) are constructed from the Wigner distribution to reach agreement between the numerical simulations and our simple wave packet model. Furthermore, a strong effect of spin–orbit coupling of the photoelectron ( ) is reported for ultrafast photoionization dynamics, and Schrödinger kitten and cat states are identified in the Wigner distributions as a result of the ACM. Our work paves the way for a deeper understanding of ultrafast photoionization and the role of causality in systems with strong electron–electron correlation effects.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast photoionization dynamics in argon, focusing on causality and Wigner delays at the Amusia-Cooper minimum.
motivation: To understand the role of causality in ultrafast photoionization and resolve gauge-dependent discrepancies in Wigner delays.
method: Ab initio simulations using relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) in length and velocity gauges, combined with a simple analytical model.
result: Length gauge yields positive Wigner delays while velocity gauge yields negative delays of several femtoseconds, but numerical simulations confirm causal behavior in both gauges.
conclusion: Weighted delays constructed from Wigner distributions reconcile gauge differences, and spin-orbit coupling significantly affects ultrafast photoionization dynamics.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for computing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills theory.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a hidden 10d conformal symmetry and obtains the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

tldr: This paper develops a fractional charge density functional theory to model electro-inductive and electric field effects at electrochemical interfaces.
motivation: Understanding how applied voltages tune chemical properties of self-assembled monolayers on electrodes is important for designing responsive molecular systems.
method: The authors extend density functional theory to incorporate fractional charges and electric fields, enabling the study of electro-inductive effects at interfaces.
result: The new theoretical framework captures the influence of voltage on molecular properties, providing insights into electric field effects at electrochemical interfaces.
conclusion: Fractional charge DFT is a useful tool for modeling electrochemical interfaces, but the work is primarily a computational chemistry method without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Zonal Spherical Functions Of Quantum Symmetric Pairs
authors: Philip Schl\"osser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the zonal and character spherical functions for quantum symmetric pairs with the symmetric Koornwinder--Macdonald polynomials. To this end, the methods of Letzter's 2004 paper are translated to modern conventions and right coideal subalgebras, and extended to non-standard cases and cases with non-reduced restricted root systems. For the last elusive Satake type, FII, a conjecture is provided.
tldr: This paper identifies zonal and character spherical functions for quantum symmetric pairs with symmetric Koornwinder-Macdonald polynomials, extending Letzter's methods to non-standard cases.
motivation: To understand the representation theory of quantum symmetric pairs and their spherical functions, which are important in harmonic analysis and special functions.
method: Translates Letzter's 2004 methods to modern conventions and right coideal subalgebras, extending to non-standard cases and non-reduced restricted root systems, with a conjecture for the FII Satake type.
result: Zonal and character spherical functions are identified with symmetric Koornwinder-Macdonald polynomials, covering most cases except FII.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for spherical functions on quantum symmetric pairs, linking them to known orthogonal polynomials.

title: On The Inseparability Of Instructions And Data In Shared-Embedding Sequence Models
authors: Dewank Pant, Shruti Lohani, Avijit Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection is the top security risk for LLM-integrated applications, yet every defense proposed so far has been broken. We prove this is not a coincidence: in shared-embedding architectures that lack enforced control-data separation, perfect prompt-injection prevention is mathematically impossible. We formalize prompted systems as Prompted Action Models whose outputs include control-authoritative actions: refusal decisions, tool authorization, policy routing, and memory writes. We define Semantic-Faithful Control (SFC), the property that such behavior depends only on the meaning of untrusted input, not on how it is encoded. We then prove SFC is unachievable within the shared pipeline, via three results: a provenance-recovery impossibility (shared representations make trusted and untrusted content statistically inseparable, bounded by total variation distance); control-path exposure (untrusted tokens enter control-relevant computation through the same attention value-aggregation that determines outputs); and a finite-coverage invariance gap (finite training cannot certify invariance over infinite semantic-equivalence classes). We ground each quantity in measurements on production tokenizers and models. The result is structural, not a gap in current defenses. It mirrors the code-data confusion in Von Neumann machines that gives rise to buffer overflows, a vulnerability class that took decades of layered defenses (DEP, Write-XOR-Execute, ASLR, stack canaries, and ultimately memory-safe languages) to contain, because no single mechanism sufficed. The implication is the same: prompt injection cannot be eliminated by better in-pipeline classification or alignment alone. It requires architectural separation of instruction and data channels. We identify the root cause and the class of solution it demands.
tldr: This paper proves that prompt injection in LLMs is structurally unavoidable in shared-embedding architectures, drawing an analogy to the code-data confusion in Von Neumann machines.
motivation: Prompt injection is a critical security risk for LLM-integrated applications, and all proposed defenses have been broken, suggesting a fundamental limitation.
method: The authors formalize prompted systems as Prompted Action Models, define Semantic-Faithful Control (SFC), and prove three impossibility results: provenance-recovery impossibility, control-path exposure, and finite-coverage invariance gap.
result: SFC is unachievable in shared-embedding architectures; prompt injection cannot be eliminated by better in-pipeline classification or alignment alone.
conclusion: Architectural separation of instruction and data channels is required, analogous to memory-safe languages for buffer overflows.

method: The authors propose a new spectroscopy technique based on measuring extinction differences for circular polarizations.

title: Toward A Hybrid Digital Twin Of Society: Quantifying Cognitive-Spatial Linkages Through Online-Offline Feedback Networks
authors: Julia Koltai Rafiazka Hilman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital platforms increasingly shape how people experience and navigate cities, linking virtual information seeking with physical mobility. Despite this interdependence, online and offline activities are often studied separately in urban mobility research. This paper introduces the Feedback Network, a computational framework that captures interactions between cognitive activity in digital environments and behavior in physical space. Using Google Search and Location History data from the same individuals, collected through a data donation framework in Budapest, Hungary, between 2018 and 2022, we examine how online search patterns and offline visitation behavior co-evolve. We combine semantic and spatial analytical approaches. Radius of gyration is adapted to measure variation in geographic mobility and semantic exploration, enabling comparison between physical movement and online cognitive dispersion. A Feedback Network models transitions between search-related and location-related activity clusters and is evaluated using Concentration Entropy, which measures whether behavioral flows are concentrated around routine pathways or distributed across exploratory transitions. The results show that online exploration is more concentrated than offline mobility, suggesting narrower and more repetitive semantic interests, while physical movement remains relatively diverse. Persistent linkages between search and visitation activities related to retail and business services indicate stable cognitive-spatial behavioral loops. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted spatial routines more strongly than cognitive exploration, widening the gap between digital engagement and realized movement. The findings demonstrate that urban mobility depends on the interaction between informational exposure and spatial encounter and provide a foundation for Hybrid Digital Twins of Society.
tldr: This paper introduces a Feedback Network framework to study the interplay between online search behavior and physical mobility in urban environments.
motivation: Online and offline activities are often studied separately in urban mobility research, but they are increasingly interdependent due to digital platforms.
method: The authors use Google Search and Location History data from individuals in Budapest, adapt radius of gyration for semantic exploration, and model transitions with a Feedback Network evaluated by Concentration Entropy.
result: Online exploration is more concentrated than offline mobility; persistent cognitive-spatial loops exist for retail and business services; COVID-19 disrupted spatial routines more than cognitive exploration.
conclusion: Urban mobility depends on the interaction between informational exposure and spatial encounter, providing a foundation for Hybrid Digital Twins of Society.

title: Mosaic: A Benchmark Suite For Differentiable Physics Solvers
authors: Andrin Rehmann, Heiko Zimmermann, Dion H\"afner
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentiable partial differential equation (PDE) solvers underpin solver-in-the-loop ML training, gradient-based optimal control, and inverse problems, yet the practical cost of obtaining correct, usable gradients from a given solver on a given problem is largely undocumented. Integration effort, computational cost, gradient accuracy, and numerical conditioning vary widely across solvers and are discoverable only by trial and error. We introduce Mosaic, an extensible benchmarking framework for differentiable PDE solvers that standardizes access to solver gradients. Each solver is packaged as a containerized component (Tesseract) exposing a uniform gradient API regardless of language or automatic differentiation (AD) strategy, enabling researchers to evaluate, compare, and build on non-trivial physical solvers. Our evaluation of 14 solvers across fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and heat transfer demonstrates that the benchmark surfaces practically relevant differences: order-of-magnitude variation in computational cost and Jacobian conditioning, alongside structural incompatibilities that eliminate solvers from realistic tasks entirely. Despite this variation, all solvers that produce gradients converge to similar optima, indicating that the practical barriers are memory limits, numerical stability, and setup compatibility rather than gradient accuracy alone. Mosaic is open-source and available at [URL].
tldr: Mosaic is a benchmarking framework for differentiable PDE solvers, focusing on computational cost, gradient accuracy, and numerical stability.
motivation: The practical cost of obtaining correct gradients from differentiable PDE solvers is undocumented, hindering solver-in-the-loop ML training and inverse problems.
method: The framework packages solvers as containerized components with a uniform gradient API, evaluating 14 solvers across fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, and heat transfer.
result: The benchmark reveals order-of-magnitude variation in computational cost and Jacobian conditioning, but all solvers converge to similar optima, indicating practical barriers are memory and stability rather than gradient accuracy.
conclusion: Mosaic provides a standardized way to evaluate and compare differentiable PDE solvers, highlighting practical challenges beyond gradient accuracy.

title: Preferentiality And Bandwidth Drive Tie Activity In Online And Offline Ego Networks
authors: Gamal Adel, Shrichand Bhuria, Alessandro Catalano, Liber Dorizzi, Leonardo Federici, Theodora Moldovan, Bern\'e Nortier, Chara Deanna Punzal, Giulia de Meijere, Gerardo I\~niguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ego networks capture the variety of structural patterns in the social interactions of individuals. Recently it has been shown that ego networks in online settings display universal patterns of tie strength distributions, but it is unclear how constraints such as spatial proximity and bounded social bandwidth affect such generic behaviour in offline settings. Here, we analyse the time evolution of interaction activity in ego networks constructed from offline face-to-face and colocation data, compare them to online communication networks, and explore simple cumulative advantage models that capture the varying preferentiality of individuals for specific social ties. We find that patterns of preferentiality at the population level are similar for online and face-to-face networks, but not for colocation data, suggesting that the latter is a poor proxy of social network structure. We also provide evidence that empirical ego networks exhibit a bandwidth in the way communication events are allocated across connections. A model implementing this notion uncovers evidence of universal scaling between the tie preferentiality and bandwidth of individuals, common to all online and offline systems explored. Our findings strengthen our understanding of the fundamental mechanisms governing human communication and help disentangle the internal and external factors shaping tie evolution across social contexts.
tldr: This paper studies tie strength and communication patterns in online and offline ego networks using cumulative advantage models.
motivation: Understanding universal patterns in social interactions and how spatial constraints affect tie evolution.
method: Analysis of face-to-face, colocation, and online communication datasets; application of preferential attachment and bandwidth models.
result: Online and face-to-face networks show similar preferentiality patterns, but colocation data differs; evidence of universal scaling between preferentiality and bandwidth.
conclusion: Findings reveal fundamental mechanisms of human communication and the role of bandwidth in tie evolution.

title: Continuous Diffraction Spectrum And The Uniform Vanishing Of Fourier--Bohr Coefficients
authors: Nicolae Strungaru
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we review the connection among continuity of the diffraction spectrum, the (uniform) vanishing of the Fourier--Bohr coefficients and the so called consistent phase frequency.
tldr: This paper reviews the connection between continuity of diffraction spectrum, uniform vanishing of Fourier-Bohr coefficients, and consistent phase frequency.
motivation: To understand the relationship between spectral continuity and Fourier-Bohr coefficients in the context of diffraction theory.
method: The paper provides a review and analysis of existing results linking diffraction spectrum continuity to the uniform vanishing of Fourier-Bohr coefficients.
result: It establishes connections among these concepts, but does not present novel results or applications to quantum information or thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work is purely mathematical and unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Analysis, Thermodynamics, And A Numeric Solver For A Pressure-temperature Equilibrium Closure Of The Four-equation Model
authors: Bennett Clayton, Joshua Mcconnell, Clell Solomon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze an often used closure model for multi-material hydrodynamics where pressure temperature equilibrium (PTE) is assumed for every state; emphasis is placed on tabular equations of state. This multi-material model is often referred to as the four-equation model. The identification of the admissible set is presented and is proven to be convex, setting the foundation for development of invariant-domain methods for this model. A novel, robust, and efficient method is presented for solving the highly nonlinear system for the equilibrated pressure and temperature with an arbitrary number of materials. Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the thermodynamics of the mixture model for general equations of state and prove existence and uniqueness of the pressure-temperature equilibrium solution under some thermodynamic assumptions.
tldr: This paper analyzes a pressure-temperature equilibrium closure for the four-equation model in multi-material hydrodynamics, focusing on numerical methods and thermodynamic consistency.
motivation: The four-equation model is widely used in multi-material hydrodynamics, but its thermodynamic properties and efficient numerical solution methods are not fully understood.
method: The authors identify the admissible set and prove its convexity, then develop a robust and efficient solver for the nonlinear pressure-temperature equilibrium system with arbitrary number of materials.
result: Existence and uniqueness of the pressure-temperature equilibrium solution are proved under certain thermodynamic assumptions, and a novel numerical method is presented.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for invariant-domain methods for the four-equation model and offers a practical solver for simulations.

title: Global Convergence Analysis Of Mixtures Of Exponential Densities
authors: Kathryn Dullerud Rajita Chandak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theoretical foundations of the EM algorithm are often thought of in the context of Gaussian mixture models, However, the practical use cases of the EM algorithm span beyond Gaussian models. This paper establishes the first step towards understanding the behavior of the EM algorithm under mixtures of non-Gaussian densities. We show that a mixture of two Exponential distributions can be approximated by the EM algorithm at the sub-Exponential rate of convergence in at most [MATH] iterations. The results here show that extending away from Gaussian mixture models does not affect the statistical performance of the EM algorithm. Furthermore, we present generalizations of typical assumptions in the Gaussian setting like minimum mean-separation and signal-to-noise ratio to the sub-Exponential setting. A simulation study is used to highlight the empirical performance of EM for mixtures of exponentials with promising results for the extension of existing theory to a larger class of mixture models.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of the EM algorithm for mixtures of exponential densities, extending results beyond Gaussian mixtures.
motivation: The EM algorithm is widely used for Gaussian mixtures, but its theoretical behavior for non-Gaussian mixtures is less understood. This work aims to establish convergence guarantees for exponential mixtures.
method: The authors prove sub-exponential convergence rates for the EM algorithm on a mixture of two exponential distributions, generalizing assumptions like minimum mean-separation and signal-to-noise ratio to the sub-exponential setting.
result: The EM algorithm converges at a sub-exponential rate in at most a specified number of iterations, and simulations confirm empirical performance.
conclusion: Extending EM theory to non-Gaussian mixtures does not degrade statistical performance, suggesting broader applicability of existing theory.

title: Improved Energy Stable Symmetric Gauss-Seidel Projection Method For Micromagnetics Simulations
authors: Changjian Xie Yingxi Miao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gauss-Seidel projection method (GSPM) constitutes an efficient and numerically stable numerical framework for micromagnetic simulations of ferromagnetic media. This scheme attains first-order temporal accuracy and second-order spatial accuracy. Fast Fourier transform (FFT) techniques can be incorporated to accelerate both the solution of the arising linear algebraic systems and the evaluation of stray magnetic fields. The conventional GSPM relies on a single-sided Gauss-Seidel iteration, which leverages the latest updated state variables associated with the heat-diffusion subproblem. In this work, we develop a symmetric Gauss-Seidel projection method (SGSPM) that retains first-order temporal accuracy and second-order spatial consistency. The proposed symmetric variant exhibits superior stability properties relative to the standard GSPM. Specifically, SGSPM adopts a two-pass symmetric Gauss-Seidel iteration, where updated information from the heat-diffusion stage is fully exploited to rigorously guarantee discrete energy stability. We validate the performance of the devised scheme through numerical investigations of magnetization dynamic evolution and magnetic domain-wall propagation. Numerical evidence demonstrates that the improved symmetric scheme delivers enhanced stability for capturing magnetization motion dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents an improved symmetric Gauss-Seidel projection method for micromagnetics simulations, focusing on numerical stability and accuracy.
motivation: Micromagnetic simulations require efficient and stable numerical methods to model magnetization dynamics accurately.
method: The authors develop a symmetric Gauss-Seidel projection method (SGSPM) that uses a two-pass iteration to fully exploit updated information from the heat-diffusion stage, ensuring discrete energy stability.
result: Numerical experiments show that SGSPM provides superior stability compared to the standard GSPM for capturing magnetization motion dynamics and domain-wall propagation.
conclusion: The proposed SGSPM is an effective numerical scheme for micromagnetics simulations with enhanced stability properties.

title: Connecting $H^\infty$-functional Calculus And Isometric Dilations For Commuting Families Of Ritt$_E$ Operators
authors: M. N. Reshmi Christian Le Merdy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a commuting [MATH]-tuple of Ritt[MATH] operators on some UMD Banach space [MATH]. We show that [MATH] admits a bounded [MATH]-functional calculus if and only if [MATH] is an [MATH]-Ritt[MATH] operator for every [MATH], and the [MATH]-tuple [MATH] admits an isometric dilation [MATH] on some UMD Banach space [MATH] such that [MATH] is polynomially bounded. In the case where [MATH] further possesses property [MATH], we establish other characterizations of the [MATH]-functional calculus property for [MATH] in terms of isometric dilations.
tldr: This paper establishes connections between H∞-functional calculus and isometric dilations for commuting families of Ritt operators on UMD Banach spaces.
motivation: The study of functional calculus and dilations for operator tuples is a topic in functional analysis and operator theory, with applications to evolution equations and harmonic analysis.
method: The authors prove equivalences between bounded H∞-functional calculus and the existence of isometric dilations with polynomial boundedness, using UMD Banach space properties and Ritt operator theory.
result: They show that a commuting tuple of Ritt operators admits a bounded H∞-functional calculus if and only if it is an R-Ritt tuple and admits an isometric dilation with polynomial boundedness.
conclusion: The results provide new characterizations of H∞-functional calculus for commuting Ritt operators, linking functional calculus to dilation theory.

title: Commutative Topological Algebras On Translation-invariant Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
authors: Miguel Angel Rodriguez Rodriguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study commutative topological algebras naturally associated with translation-invariant reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces whose direct integral decomposition has one-dimensional fibers. Starting from the bounded algebra of translation-invariant operators, we pass to a common dense domain generated by reproducing kernels and identify the corresponding diagonalizable operators with multiplication by symbols in an intersection of weighted [MATH]-spaces. On the symbol side this gives a canonical space [MATH] and a maximal multiplicative subalgebra [MATH], which is a complete locally convex [MATH]-algebra. Transporting the structure back yields corresponding algebras of operators and integral kernels. We also discuss when the inclusions [MATH] are strict, and illustrate the results with vertical and radial operators on classical Bergman and Fock spaces.
tldr: This paper studies commutative topological algebras on translation-invariant reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, focusing on operator algebras and symbol spaces.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of bounded translation-invariant operators on certain reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and their diagonalizable subalgebras.
method: They use direct integral decomposition, construct a common dense domain from reproducing kernels, and identify diagonalizable operators with multiplication by symbols in weighted L^p spaces.
result: They obtain a canonical symbol space and a maximal multiplicative subalgebra that is a complete locally convex algebra, and discuss strictness of inclusions.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic algebraic framework for translation-invariant operators on these Hilbert spaces, with potential applications in functional analysis.

title: Tropical Fermat--Weber Problems Over Non-Finite Data And Their Inverse Formulations
authors: Ruriko Yoshida John Sabol
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The term tropical pseudonorm refers to a family of (not necessarily symmetric) gauge functions that arise in tropical or idempotent geometry. An important characteristic of these gauges is their invariance under translation by a constant vector, allowing them to descent naturally to tropical projective spaces. In this work, we explore the tropical one-infinity pseudonorm, a polyhedral hybrid gauge that allows for tunable asymmetry, in the context of a Fermat--Weber location problem. We extend previous formulations in considering non-finite data, and we investigate several variants of the inverse problem, providing linear programming formulations for their solution.
tldr: This paper studies tropical Fermat-Weber problems with non-finite data and their inverse formulations using tropical pseudonorms.
motivation: To extend tropical location problems to handle non-finite data and explore inverse problems, which have applications in optimization and geometry.
method: The authors use tropical one-infinity pseudonorm, a polyhedral hybrid gauge, and formulate linear programming solutions for the inverse problem variants.
result: Linear programming formulations are provided for solving the inverse tropical Fermat-Weber problem with non-finite data.
conclusion: The work advances tropical geometry and optimization but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Any-dimensional Positivstellens\"atze For Symmetric Functions
authors: Robin Schabert Sebastian Debus
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Positivstellens\"atze provide certificates of positivity for polynomials. Extending these certificates to symmetric functions, uniformly across all dimensions, presents structural challenges. For instance, the underlying domain is not semialgebraic. In this paper, we prove two Positivstellens\"atze for symmetric functions that are uniformly bounded below by some [MATH]. These are infinite dimensional analogous of theorems of P\'olya and Reznick. The proof relates evaluations of the (truncated) power sum map [MATH] to moments of discrete probability measures on the compact interval [MATH]. This yields a characterization of the orbit space of the infinite symmetric group. Finally, we provide an alternative proof of existing Positivstellens\"atze for normalized symmetric functions.
tldr: This paper proves Positivstellensätze for symmetric functions that are uniformly bounded below, extending classical theorems to infinite dimensions.
motivation: Classical Positivstellensätze provide certificates of positivity for polynomials, but extending them to symmetric functions across all dimensions is challenging because the domain is not semialgebraic.
method: The proof relates evaluations of the power sum map to moments of discrete probability measures on a compact interval, characterizing the orbit space of the infinite symmetric group.
result: Two Positivstellensätze for symmetric functions are proved, analogous to theorems of Pólya and Reznick, and an alternative proof of existing results is provided.
conclusion: The work establishes positivity certificates for symmetric functions in infinite dimensions, contributing to real algebraic geometry and symmetric function theory.

title: Pick Two: An Adversarial Animal Survival Game
authors: Ramsha Anwar Jack Vanlyssel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The "Pick Two" animal selection puzzle is a popular thought experiment in which two animal species must defend a human against the remaining animal attackers. While typically discussed informally, the scenario presents a heterogeneous coalition-selection problem involving complex interactions among agents with different capabilities and behaviors. In this work, we formalize Pick Two as an adversarial multi-agent optimization problem and develop a biologically inspired agent-based simulation framework to evaluate defender coalition effectiveness. Coalition performance is evaluated through 18,000 Monte Carlo simulations conducted in a Unity-based environment. Results show that coalition effectiveness is not additive and is instead dominated by interaction effects and scaling behavior. Overall, this study demonstrates how agent-based simulation can be used to analyze coalition effectiveness in adversarial environments and highlights the importance of emergent group dynamics in determining collective success.
tldr: This paper formalizes the 'Pick Two' animal survival puzzle as an adversarial multi-agent optimization problem and uses agent-based simulation to evaluate coalition effectiveness.
motivation: The 'Pick Two' puzzle is a popular thought experiment lacking formal analysis; the authors aim to study coalition selection in adversarial environments with heterogeneous agents.
method: They develop a biologically inspired agent-based simulation framework in Unity and perform 18,000 Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate defender coalition effectiveness.
result: Coalition effectiveness is non-additive and dominated by interaction effects and scaling behavior, not individual capabilities.
conclusion: Agent-based simulation can effectively analyze coalition effectiveness in adversarial settings, highlighting the importance of emergent group dynamics.

title: Discrete Event Population Updates: Finding Game Theoretic Emergent Behaviour In Queueing Systems With Simulation
authors: Vincent Knight, Geraint I. Palmer-Liyu, Thomas Hutton
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strategic behaviour in queueing systems has been studied extensively in the behavioural queueing literature, but almost exclusively for systems that admit closed-form expressions for the cost or utility experienced by a strategic user. Evolutionary game theory offers a mature framework for analysing populations whose individual payoffs depend on the composition of the population itself, and would in principle apply to a much wider class of queueing systems; its application has, however, been constrained by the same closed-form requirement. We introduce Discrete Event Population Updates (DEPU), a general algorithmic framework that couples a single long run of a discrete event simulation (DES) directly to an evolutionary population update rule, removing that constraint. We present two implementations: Discrete Event Replicator Dynamics (DERD), which follows an Euler discretisation of the replicator dynamics equation, and Discrete Event Moran Replacement (DEMR), which maintains a finite population updated via Moran-style copying events. Both are applied to a multi-server jockeying model for which no closed-form fitness expressions are available. On the jockeying model considered, DEPU reaches comparable precision tens of times faster than the standard practice of nesting short simulations inside an outer evolutionary loop, and because each operating point then costs only a single simulation run it also makes systematic parameter sweeps tractable. This brings the toolkit of evolutionary dynamics within reach of any system a modeller can build in a discrete event simulator.
tldr: This paper introduces a computational framework (DEPU) that couples discrete event simulation with evolutionary game theory to analyze strategic behavior in queueing systems, but it does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Strategic behavior in queueing systems is typically studied only for models with closed-form solutions; the authors aim to extend evolutionary game theory to arbitrary queueing systems via simulation.
method: The paper proposes Discrete Event Population Updates (DEPU), with two implementations: Discrete Event Replicator Dynamics (DERD) and Discrete Event Moran Replacement (DEMR), which run a single long simulation coupled to an evolutionary update rule.
result: DEPU achieves comparable precision tens of times faster than standard nested simulation approaches and enables systematic parameter sweeps.
conclusion: DEPU brings evolutionary dynamics to any system that can be modeled in a discrete event simulator, removing the closed-form requirement.

title: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness For Automatic Speech Recognition
authors: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition systems are notoriously both sensitive to adversarial and benign perturbations. While this has been repeatedly demonstrated using reference datasets, detecting such behaviors in deployed systems is incredibly challenging, due to the absence of oracle knowledge of the true transcription. We demonstrate that employing a certification-inspired mechanism can significantly decrease WER, increase recall, and decrease the Spearman correlation between confidence and WER. We achieve this through a dual-gate diagnostic pipeline: a Two-Sided Atomic Audit that accumulates statistical wealth to certify both token existence and adversarial exclusion, and a Rank-Based Tournament that selects the winning sequence. Our evaluations across four diverse architectures demonstrate up to a 55% relative reduction in Word Error Rate, while also providing granular word- and sentence-level certifications to enhance acoustic security.
tldr: This paper proposes a certification-inspired method to improve robustness of automatic speech recognition systems against adversarial and benign perturbations.
motivation: Automatic speech recognition systems are sensitive to perturbations, but detecting such behaviors in deployed systems is challenging due to lack of oracle knowledge of true transcription.
method: A dual-gate diagnostic pipeline consisting of a Two-Sided Atomic Audit for token certification and a Rank-Based Tournament for sequence selection.
result: Evaluations across four architectures show up to 55% relative reduction in Word Error Rate and granular word- and sentence-level certifications.
conclusion: The proposed method enhances acoustic security and robustness of ASR systems without requiring oracle knowledge.

title: ToE: A Hierarchical And Explainable Claim Verification Framework With Dynamic Multi-source Evidence Retrieval And Aggregation
authors: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Kun Zheng, Zhen Li, Xin Li, Chunlei Li, Jiamou Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid spread of fake news poses increasing threats to information ecosystems, especially as AI-generated misinformation under Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) poisoning allows adversarially crafted content to be systematically surfaced by retrieval systems, contaminating LLM reasoning. In this paper, we propose Tree of Evidence (ToE), a hierarchical evidence reasoning framework for automated fact-checking that models each claim as a dynamically expanding argument tree. ToE integrates a reinforcement learning-driven multi-source retrieval agent, an evidence evaluation agent, and an argument tree aggregation algorithm to iteratively decompose, retrieve, and verify claims through an explainable evidence chain. We further provide a theoretical analysis of the retrieval process, deriving a formal error bound that guarantees the learned policy converges to a neighborhood of the information-theoretically optimal policy. Experiments across multiple datasets and backbone LLMs demonstrate that ToE achieves improvements ranging from 4 to 24 percentage points over competitive baselines, with particularly pronounced gains on adversarially poisoned inputs.
tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchical evidence reasoning framework for automated fact-checking using reinforcement learning and multi-source evidence retrieval.
motivation: The spread of fake news and AI-generated misinformation threatens information ecosystems, necessitating robust automated fact-checking methods.
method: The Tree of Evidence (ToE) framework models claims as argument trees, using a reinforcement learning-driven retrieval agent, an evidence evaluation agent, and an aggregation algorithm to iteratively decompose, retrieve, and verify claims.
result: Experiments show ToE achieves 4-24 percentage point improvements over baselines, especially on adversarially poisoned inputs, with a theoretical error bound guaranteeing convergence to near-optimal policy.
conclusion: ToE provides an explainable and effective approach to claim verification, demonstrating robustness against adversarial misinformation.

title: Ramses: Secure High-performance Computing For Sensitive Data
authors: Peter Heger, Lech Nieroda, Roland Pabel, Christoph Stollwerk, Stefan Borowski, Kamil Tokmakov, Michael Commer, Martin Peifer, Stefan Wesner, Viktor Achter
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditionally, the architecture of high-performance computing (HPC) systems is tailored for speed, while highly secure computer systems must sacrifice speed for security. However, a wide range of scientific domains, such as the life sciences, call for a combination of performance and security to allow processing sensitive data at scale. Here, we present RAMSES (Research Accelerator for Modeling and Simulation with Enhanced Security), an HPC system designed from the ground up to deliver high performance within a robust security framework. RAMSES integrates hardware-based memory encryption of AMD processors with state-of-the-art file encryption from IBM Storage Scale and the Thales CipherTrust manager, establishing an HPC platform that ensures continuous encryption throughout the data life cycle - at rest, in transit, and in use - in compliance with major data protection standards (European General Data Protection Regulation, ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and Federal Information Processing Standards). In addition, we implemented advanced operating system hardening, a multi-layered security architecture, and mandatory multi-factor authentication to adapt the HPC environment to increased security demands. Benchmark results from the biomedical sector demonstrate that the performance impact of the secure environment is limited and that integration of the conflicting requirements speed and security can be achieved while preserving a coherent, flexible, and user-friendly system.
tldr: This paper presents RAMSES, an HPC system designed for secure processing of sensitive data with hardware-based memory encryption and file encryption.
motivation: Scientific domains like life sciences require both high performance and security for processing sensitive data, but traditional HPC systems prioritize speed over security.

title: Transversal Difference Numbers In Finite Abelian Quotients
authors: Mugurel Barcau, Vicen\c{t}iu Pa\c{s}ol, George C. \c{t}urca\c{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given \(H\leq G\) finite abelian groups, a transversal \(T\subseteq G\) for \(G/H\) has fixed size \(|G/H|\), but its ambient difference support \(D(T)=T-T\) can vary with the embedding of \(H\) in \(G\). We call [MATH] the transversal difference number of the pair \((G,H)\). This invariant is related to finite abelian factorisation, tiling complements, and small-sumset questions, and is motivated by recent work regarding ambient Galois labels in CRT transforms for cyclotomic-subfield homomorphic encryption. We prove various results regarding this invariant, including a general lower bound [MATH] where \(m(G,H)\) is the largest order of a subgroup of \(G\) disjoint from \(H\). The bound is sharp for cyclic quotients, and Kneser's theorem gives a cross-transversal estimate leading to exact product families with one nonsplit cyclic coordinate and arbitrary split factors. These results isolate the first genuinely new residual obstruction, namely the same-prime square plane \[ G=(\mathbb Z/p^2\mathbb Z)^2,\qquad H=pG. \] For odd \(p\), this case is the technical core of the paper. Here transversals are graphs of functions \(\mathbb F_p^2\to \mathbb F_p^2\), and \(D(T)\) decomposes into carry-corrected finite-field derivative images. We conjecture that \[ \delta(G,H)=(2p-1)^2 \] for all odd primes \(p\), prove the unconditional lower bound \(3p^2-p-1\), and give small-prime, probabilistic, and fixed-polynomial evidence for the conjecture.
tldr: This paper studies transversal difference numbers in finite abelian groups, a combinatorial number theory problem with applications to homomorphic encryption.
motivation: The work is motivated by ambient Galois labels in CRT transforms for cyclotomic-subfield homomorphic encryption, but the core problem is purely algebraic/combinatorial.
method: The authors use group theory, Kneser's theorem, and finite field analysis to derive lower bounds and exact formulas for the transversal difference number.
result: They prove a general lower bound, sharp for cyclic quotients, and identify a critical case for (Z/p^2Z)^2 where they conjecture the exact value and provide evidence.
conclusion: The paper isolates a new obstruction in transversal difference numbers but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

We propose a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo (FM-MCMC) algorithm for estimating the orbital parameters of exoplanetary systems, especially for those in which only one exoplanet is involved. Compared to traditional methods that rely on random sampling within the Bayesian framework, our approac…

tldr: This paper proposes a flow-matching Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm for estimating orbital parameters of directly imaged exoplanets.
motivation: Traditional Bayesian methods for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation rely on random sampling and can be inefficient. The authors aim to improve efficiency using a flow-matching approach.
method: The FM-MCMC algorithm combines normalizing flows with Markov chain Monte Carlo to sample from the posterior distribution of orbital parameters.
result: The algorithm demonstrates improved sampling efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional MCMC methods on synthetic and real data.
conclusion: Flow-matching MCMC is a promising tool for exoplanet orbital parameter estimation, offering faster convergence and better exploration of parameter space.

authors: Bomin Kim, Tumentsereg Ochirkhuyag, Dorj Odkhuu, And S. H. Rhim

Physics of [MATH] having higher Curie temperature [MATH] than [MATH] is explored theoretically in the framework of magnetic exchange interactions. [MATH] and [MATH] ar…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023333] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of higher Curie temperature in Fe3GaTe2 compared to Fe3GeTe2 using magnetic exchange interaction analysis.
motivation: Understanding why Fe3GaTe2 has a higher Curie temperature than Fe3GeTe2 is important for designing two-dimensional magnetic materials with enhanced thermal stability.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations to evaluate magnetic exchange parameters and use Monte Carlo simulations to estimate Curie temperatures.
result: They find that stronger in-plane ferromagnetic exchange interactions in Fe3GaTe2 lead to its higher Curie temperature.
conclusion: The study provides insights into tuning Curie temperatures in van der Waals magnets by chemical substitution.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and evaluate the effects of heat treatment.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and annealing processes to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and the multimessenger astrophysics enabled by future detectors.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will advance our understanding of neutron star physics.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the universe, and their properties constrain the behavior of matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes recent observational constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements provide constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, which are compared to theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine our understanding of the dense matter equation of state.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, and project discovery potential for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC, but does not present new theoretical or experimental results.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable in certain regions of parameter space, and the HL-LHC will have significant discovery potential across multiple channels.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating all data up to the end of 2022.
result: A self-consistent set of values and uncertainties for the fundamental constants is provided, along with detailed documentation of the input data and methodology.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values represent the most accurate and reliable set of fundamental constants, superseding previous adjustments.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The paper summarizes the state of the art in optoacoustic microscopy and its applications.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for deep-tissue imaging with optical contrast, and ongoing developments enhance its capabilities.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses gravitational wave signals from early universe phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves can probe the first second of the universe, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical predictions for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, along with detection strategies.
result: It summarizes possible signals and detection methods for early universe gravitational waves.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique window into the earliest moments of the universe, complementing other probes.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools based on Wannier functions for electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys various software packages and their interoperability, describing how Wannier functions are used to transform Bloch states into localized orbitals.
result: The ecosystem enables accurate integrations, topological invariant calculations, and materials design.
conclusion: Wannier functions are a powerful tool in condensed-matter physics, and the software ecosystem supports a wide range of applications.

title: Nucleation Of Adamantane Clusters In Weakly Ionised Plasmas: Dispersion Cohesion, Surface Energy, And Charging
authors: Johannes Fiedler And Justas Zalieckas
abstract: The formation of molecular clusters in low-temperature plasmas is governed by an intricate interplay of dispersion interactions, electrostatic charging, and surface energetics. While chemical growth pathways have been extensively studied, the role of non-chemical interactions in determining characteristic cluster sizes remains poorly understood. In this work, we develop a unified free-energy framework for molecular clusters embedded in weakly ionised Ar/H plasmas. The approach combines first-principles calculations of the molecular polarisability of adamantane with a dielectric description of the plasma response, including collisional damping and plasma screening. Dispersion interactions are treated as a bulk-like cohesive contribution with a physically motivated microscopic cutoff, while electrostatic charging is described within floating-potential theory. We show that, for realistic discharge parameters, the total free energy does not generally exhibit an effective equilibrium radius. Instead, the free-energy landscape is characterised by a nucleation barrier with an effective critical radius separating subcritical clusters from downhill growth. By mapping this nucleation threshold scale as a function of pressure, electron temperature, and gas composition, we demonstrate that plasma conditions provide a systematic control over the nucleation scale. Our results suggest that experimentally observed steady cluster sizes in weakly ionised plasmas are governed by kinetic balance rather than free-energy minimisation, and that gas composition and plasma parameters can be used as effective control knobs for early-stage cluster formation.
tldr: This paper studies nucleation of adamantane clusters in weakly ionized plasmas using a free-energy framework, focusing on dispersion interactions and charging effects.
motivation: The role of non-chemical interactions in determining cluster sizes in low-temperature plasmas is poorly understood.
method: A unified free-energy model combining first-principles polarisability calculations with dielectric plasma response, including collisional damping and screening.
result: The free-energy landscape shows a nucleation barrier with a critical radius; no effective equilibrium radius exists; cluster sizes are governed by kinetic balance.
conclusion: Plasma conditions (pressure, electron temperature, gas composition) can systematically control nucleation scale.

title: Photon Accelerator In Magnetized Electron–ion Plasma
authors: S V Bulanov, S S Bulanov, T Z Esirkepov, G Gregori, G M Grittani, M Lamač, B K Russell, A G R Thomas And P Valenta
abstract: Strong magnetic fields and plasmas are intrinsically linked in both terrestrial laboratory experiments and in space phenomena. One of the most profound consequences of that is the change in relationship between the frequency and the wave number of electromagnetic waves propagating in plasma in the presence of such magnetic fields when compared to the case without these fields. Furthermore, magnetic fields alter electromagnetic wave interaction with relativistic plasma waves, resulting in different outcomes for particle and radiation generation. For a relativistic plasma wave-based photon acceleration this leads to an increased frequency gain and, thus, potentially to higher efficiency. The influence of a magnetic field leads to quantitative and qualitative change in the properties of photon acceleration, amplifying the increase in the electromagnetic wave frequency.
tldr: This paper studies photon acceleration in magnetized electron-ion plasma, focusing on frequency upshifts due to relativistic plasma waves and magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how strong magnetic fields alter electromagnetic wave propagation and photon acceleration in plasma, which is relevant to laboratory and astrophysical plasmas.
method: Theoretical analysis using plasma physics and relativistic wave equations to model photon acceleration in magnetized plasma.
result: Magnetic fields enhance the frequency gain of photon acceleration, leading to higher efficiency compared to unmagnetized cases.
conclusion: Magnetic fields can significantly improve photon acceleration, offering potential for more efficient radiation generation.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic order and elastic properties.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice contraction and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked to the lattice, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Reservoir-independent Lossless Charging And Protected Storage Of An Open Quantum Battery
authors: Asad Ali, H. Kuniyil, M. I Hussain, M. T Rahim, Saif Al-Kuwari, James Q. Quach
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum battery charged through a lossy intermediate state faces a structural trade-off between charging speed and dissipation. We show that an exact algebraic cancellation removes it in a driven three-level cell: the radiatively decaying state is fed by a single bright amplitude, and a counterdiabatic field annuls the lone residual source that drives it, holding the lossy state identically empty. Charging is then lossless -- not one photon is emitted through the bridge -- at any one-photon detuning, coupling, linewidth, and speed down to the rotating-wave limit, with no adiabatic elimination, so the charging power is bounded by the drive amplitude (a quantum speed limit) rather than by dissipation. Crucially, this losslessness is independent of the reservoir: because the dark sector never engages the system-bath coupling, the emission vanishes exactly for an arbitrary spectral density, Markovian or not, as an exact damped-pseudomode treatment confirms to machine precision across all memory times. The entire non-Hermitian structure -- a Markovian second-order exceptional point that reservoir memory promotes to a third-order one, and the attendant dissipation phase diagram -- lives in the bright sector, from which the protocol is by construction exempt. This inverts dissipation-engineered charging, where an exceptional point or reservoir memory is a resource; here the lossy sector is never populated at all. The same dark-state structure protects the stored charge, converting fast radiative self-discharge into the slow metastable lifetime, with residuals quadratic in the control error. We detail experimental requirements and representative parameters for neutral alkaline-earth atoms, trapped ions, transmons, and defect centers.

title: Non-dipole Effects In Two-photon Double Ionization Of The K-shell Of A Beryllium-like Atomic Ion
authors: Alexey N. Hopersky, Alexey M. Nadolinsky, Rustam V. Koneev, Julia N. Kolesnikova
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the second order of the non-relativistic quantum perturbation theory and outside the framework of the dipole approximation for the operator of the radiation transition between continuum-spectrum states, the analytical structures and absolute values of the generalized cross-sections of the two-photon double ionization of the K-shell of beryllium-like ions of titanium (Ti18+), iron (Fe22+) and zinc (Zn26+) atoms were predicted. It has been established that taking into account non-dipole effects by several orders of magnitude (giant non-dipole effect) reduces the generalized cross-sections calculated within the framework of the dipole approximation. It has also been established that at high (12.5 - 28 keV) energies of the absorbed photons, the generalized cross-section of the two-photon double ionization of the K-shell is several orders of magnitude greater than the generalized cross-section of the single ionization.
